  grace_period_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this premium allocation was applied during the policy\'s grace period. When True, the allocation is a late payment that prevented lapse. Critical for grace period management, lapse administration, and regulatory compliance reporting.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this allocation record was most recently modified, such as during a reversal, adjustment, or status change. Supports audit trail and change tracking requirements.']
  mec_test_status varchar [note: 'The result of the Modified Endowment Contract (MEC) 7-pay test for this premium allocation. PASS = premium does not cause the policy to become a MEC; FAIL = premium causes or contributes to MEC classification; NOT_APPLICABLE = MEC testing not required for this product type. MEC classification has significant tax implications under IRC Section 7702A.']
  modal_premium_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The scheduled modal premium amount for the policy at the time of this allocation, representing the total premium due for the billing mode (annual, semi-annual, quarterly, monthly). Used to validate that the total allocation equals the expected modal premium.']
  nar_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The Net Amount at Risk (NAR) used in the COI charge calculation for this allocation period, representing the difference between the death benefit and the policy account value. Applicable for UL/IUL/VUL products when component_type is COI.']
  nsf_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the premium payment associated with this allocation was returned due to Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF). When True, the allocation is typically reversed and the policy may enter a grace period. Supports NSF handling and lapse administration workflows.']
  payment_method varchar [note: 'The payment instrument or method used to remit the premium payment from which this allocation was derived. EFT_ACH = Electronic Funds Transfer via ACH; CHECK = paper check; CREDIT_CARD = credit/debit card; WIRE = wire transfer; DIRECT_BILL = direct billing to policyholder; LIST_BILL = employer or group list billing.']
  policy_number varchar [note: 'The externally-known policy contract number associated with this allocation. Denormalized for operational reporting and reconciliation without requiring a join to the policy table.']
  policy_year varchar [note: 'The policy year (1-based integer) in which this premium allocation falls, calculated from the policy issue date. Used for COI rate determination, MEC 7-pay test tracking, DAC amortization, and actuarial experience studies.']
  product_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the insurance product type associated with the policy for this allocation. Determines applicable allocation logic: UL/IUL/VUL products require COI and expense load splits; WL and TERM products allocate entirely to base premium. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WL|UL|IUL|VUL|YRT|TERM|SPIA|FIA|ANNUITY — promote to reference product]']
  reinstatement_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this premium allocation is associated with a policy reinstatement payment, where a lapsed policy is being restored to in-force status. Reinstatement allocations may include back-premium and interest charges.']
  reinsurance_ceded_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a portion of the premium associated with this allocation has been ceded to a reinsurer under an active reinsurance treaty. When True, the corresponding reinsurance premium cession will be recorded in the reinsurance domain.']
  reversal_reason_code varchar [note: 'Code indicating the reason this allocation was reversed when allocation_status is REVERSED. NSF = Non-Sufficient Funds return; PAYMENT_ERROR = incorrect payment amount; POLICY_CANCEL = policy cancelled retroactively; BILLING_CORRECTION = billing system correction; DUPLICATE = duplicate payment reversal; REINSTATEMENT_REVERSAL = reinstatement declined. Null when allocation has not been reversed.']
  rider_code varchar [note: 'Industry-standard code identifying the specific rider to which this allocation applies when component_type is RIDER_PREMIUM. ADB = Accidental Death Benefit; AWL = Automatic Waiver of Premium; CAR = Company Action Rider; LTC = Long-Term Care; DI = Disability Income; GMDB/GMWB/GMIB/GMAB = Guaranteed Minimum benefit riders; WP = Waiver of Premium. Null when component_type is not RIDER_PREMIUM. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ADB|AWL|CAR|LTC|DI|GMDB|GMWB|GMIB|GMAB|WP — promote to reference product]']

  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational source system that originated this premium allocation record (e.g., SAPIENS_BILLING, FAST_PAS, MAJESCO_BILLING). Supports data lineage, reconciliation between systems, and ETL audit trails in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  tax_qualified_indicator boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this premium allocation is associated with a tax-qualified plan (e.g., 401(k), IRA, pension plan).   period_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the grace period based on its governing basis. \'standard\' reflects the default NAIC model regulation grace period (30-31 days). \'extended\' reflects a grace period longer than standard, granted by company policy or state mandate. \'state_mandated\' reflects a grace period required by a specific state DOI regulation. \'contractual\' reflects a grace period defined within the policy contract terms.']

  premium_due_date date [note: 'The original scheduled premium due date that was missed or insufficiently paid, triggering the grace period. Used to reconcile the grace period against the premium billing schedule.']
  prior_grace_count varchar [note: 'The number of prior grace period events on this policy before the current grace period. A high count indicates a pattern of payment difficulty and may trigger enhanced lapse prevention workflows or underwriting review.']
  product_type varchar [note: 'The type of life insurance or annuity product associated with the policy under grace period. Determines applicable grace period rules, state regulatory requirements, and resolution options (e.g., APL eligibility). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: whole_life|term_life|universal_life|variable_universal_life|indexed_universal_life|annuity|disability_income|long_term_care — promote to reference product]']

  resolution_outcome varchar [note: 'The final resolution outcome of the grace period. \'paid\' indicates the outstanding premium was paid in full within the grace period. \'lapsed\' indicates the policy lapsed due to non-payment. \'apl_triggered\' indicates an Automatic Premium Loan (APL) was applied to cover the outstanding premium. \'reinstated\' indicates the policy was reinstated after lapse. \'waived\' indicates the premium was waived (e.g., due to disability waiver rider).']
  second_notice_date date [note: 'The date on which the second or follow-up grace period notice was sent to the policyholder. Some states require multiple notices during the grace period window. Null if only one notice is required or sent.']
  source_system varchar [note: 'The operational billing or policy administration system from which this grace period record originated. Supports data lineage, ETL reconciliation, and multi-system integration in the lakehouse silver layer.']
  source_system_reference varchar [note: 'The native identifier or reference number assigned to this grace period record in the originating operational system (e.g., Sapiens BillingPro internal grace period ID). Supports cross-system reconciliation and ETL traceability.']
  start_date date [note: 'The date on which the grace period commenced, typically the day after the premium due date when payment was not received. This is the principal business event date for the grace period lifecycle.']
  state_of_issue varchar [note: 'The two-letter US state code of the state in which the policy was issued. Determines the applicable state DOI grace period regulations, required notice timelines, and lapse rules that govern this grace period record.']
  third_party_notice_date date [note: 'The date on which the lapse notice was sent to the designated third party (e.g., assignee, ILIT trustee). Null if no third party notice is required or if it has not yet been sent.']
  third_party_notice_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a lapse notice must also be sent to a designated third party (e.g., assignee, collateral assignee, or irrevocable beneficiary) per state DOI regulations or policy contract terms. Relevant for ILIT (Irrevocable Life Insurance Trust) and collateral assignment scenarios.']
  trigger_reason varchar [note: 'The specific reason that initiated the grace period. \'missed_payment\' indicates no payment was received by the due date. \'insufficient_payment\' indicates a partial payment was received but did not meet the required premium amount. \'nsf_return\' indicates a Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) check was returned. \'eft_failure\' indicates an Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT)/ACH payment failed. \'check_return\' indicates a physical check was returned unpaid.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this grace period record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Tracks the most recent status change, notice sent, or resolution update for audit trail purposes.']
  waiver_of_premium_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a Waiver of Premium rider (e.g., Automatic Waiver of Premium — AWL, or disability waiver) is active on the policy at the time of the grace period. If true, the outstanding premium may be waived, affecting the resolution outcome.']

  Note: 'Transactional record tracking the grace period status for a policy following a missed or insufficient premium payment. Captures grace period start date, grace period end date (typically 30-31 days per NAIC model regulation, varies by state), grace period type, triggering bill reference, outstanding premium amount required to cure, notices sent (with dates), and resolution outcome (paid, lapsed, APL triggered, reinstated). SSOT for grace period administration per state DOI requirements. Supports regulatory notice timeline compliance and lapse prevention workflows.'

Tracks whether the event is open and awaiting resolution, pending re-presentment, resolved via manual payment, or has triggered lapse initiation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|resolved|pending_representment|lapse_initiated|waived|written_off — promote to reference product]']
  lapse_initiation_date date [note: 'The date on which the policy lapse process was formally initiated as a result of the unresolved NSF event. Null if the NSF was remediated before lapse. Triggers lapse administration workflows in the Policy Administration System.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for billing operations staff to record additional context about the NSF event, such as customer communication details, special handling instructions, or escalation notes. Supports customer service and audit review workflows.']
  notification_channel varchar [note: 'The communication channel used to deliver the NSF notification to the policyholder. State regulations may mandate specific notification methods (e.g., first-class mail). Supports compliance reporting and customer communication analytics.']
  nsf_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the bank returned the payment as Non-Sufficient Funds. This is the principal business event date used to trigger grace period calculations and state-mandated notification timelines.']
  nsf_fee_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Dollar amount of the NSF fee assessed to the policyholder\'s billing account as a result of the returned payment. Fee amounts are governed by state regulations and policy contract terms. May be zero if the insurer waives the fee.']
  nsf_fee_waived boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the NSF fee was waived for this event. True if the fee was waived (e.g., first-time occurrence, hardship waiver, or state regulatory requirement). Supports fee waiver reporting and customer service analytics.']
  nsf_fee_waiver_reason varchar [note: 'Reason code explaining why the NSF fee was waived. Applicable only when nsf_fee_waived is True. Supports audit compliance and waiver pattern analysis.']
  nsf_notification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a state-mandated NSF notification must be sent to the policyholder. State regulations vary in their NSF notification requirements. True triggers the notification workflow in the CRM and customer engagement platform.']
  nsf_notification_sent_date date [note: 'The date on which the state-mandated NSF notification was sent to the policyholder. Null if notification has not yet been sent. Critical for demonstrating compliance with state notification timing requirements.']
  nsf_occurrence_count varchar [note: 'Cumulative count of NSF events recorded for this policy over its lifetime at the time this event was created. Used to identify chronic NSF patterns, assess lapse risk, and determine fee waiver eligibility (e.g., first-occurrence waiver policies).']
  nsf_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier for the NSF event, typically assigned by the billing system or bank. Used for correspondence, state NSF notifications, and audit trails.']
  payment_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The gross dollar amount of the original premium payment that was returned NSF. Represents the full EFT/ACH debit amount attempted, which may include base premium, rider premiums, and Cost of Insurance (COI) charges.']
  payment_method varchar [note: 'The payment instrument type used for the original payment that was returned NSF. Most NSF events originate from EFT/ACH transactions, but returned checks and other instruments are also captured.']
  policy_status_at_nsf varchar [note: 'The status of the life insurance policy at the time the NSF event was recorded. Critical for determining the appropriate remediation workflow — an already-lapsed policy requires reinstatement processing rather than grace period management.']
  remediation_action varchar [note: 'The action taken to resolve the NSF event. Re-presentment submits the ACH transaction again; manual payment accepts an alternative payment; Automatic Premium Loan (APL) uses policy cash value to cover the premium; lapse_initiated records that no remediation occurred. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: representment|manual_payment|apl_triggered|lapse_initiated|reinstated|waived|pending|write_off — promote to reference product]']
  remediation_date date [note: 'The date on which the NSF event was successfully resolved through the recorded remediation action. Null if the event remains unresolved. Used to measure time-to-resolution and grace period utilization.']
  representment_count varchar [note: 'Number of times the original ACH/EFT payment has been re-presented to the bank following the initial NSF return. NACHA rules limit re-presentments to two attempts after the original return. Supports NACHA compliance monitoring.']
  representment_date date [note: 'The date on which the most recent ACH re-presentment was submitted to the bank. Null if no re-presentment has been attempted. Used to track NACHA re-presentment timing compliance.']
  representment_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the ACH re-presentment attempt for this NSF event. Tracks whether re-presentment succeeded, was returned again, or has reached the NACHA-mandated re-presentment limit.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational billing system that originated this NSF event record (e.g., SAPIENS_BILLING, MAJESCO_BILLING). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer and multi-system reconciliation.']
  state_code varchar [note: 'Two-letter US state code representing the situs state of the policy at the time of the NSF event. Determines which state\'s NSF notification requirements, grace period mandates, and fee regulations apply.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the NSF event record, reflecting status changes, remediation actions, re-presentment attempts, or notification updates. Supports change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of a Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) or returned payment event, capturing the original payment reference, NSF date, bank return reason code, NSF fee assessed, grace period impact, policy status at NSF, and remediation action taken (re-presentment, manual payment, lapse initiation). Critical for EFT/ACH payment management and state-mandated NSF notification compliance.'
}

Table billing.eft_authorization {

This FK links the authorization to the billing_account it serves. While eft_authorization already links to po']
  authorization_document_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to document.document. Business justification: EFT authorizations require signed bank authorization forms, ACH mandate documents for regulatory compliance and audit. Real business process: payment processing compliance, NACHA requirements, audit t']

  party_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the party (policyholder, group sponsor, or third-party payer) who owns the bank account and has authorized the EFT debit.']
  account_token varchar [note: 'Tokenized reference to the full bank account number stored in a PCI-compliant vault. Used by the ACH origination system to retrieve the actual account number at transaction time without storing it in the billing database.']
  account_type varchar [note: 'Type of bank account from which premiums will be debited. Determines the SEC code and NACHA transaction class used in ACH file generation.']
  apl_authorized boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the policyholder has authorized the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) feature as a fallback when EFT collection fails and the policy has sufficient cash value. When True, the billing system may trigger an APL to prevent lapse.']
  authorization_channel varchar [note: 'Channel through which the payer submitted the EFT authorization. Agent = through licensed agent; Online portal = self-service web/mobile; Call center = telephone; Mail = paper form mailed in; Branch = in-person at office.']
  authorization_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the payer signed or electronically consented to the EFT debit authorization. This is the legal consent date required by NACHA and Regulation E for audit purposes.']
  authorization_method varchar [note: 'Method by which the payer granted authorization for EFT debits. Wet signature = paper form; E-sign = electronic signature; Voice = recorded verbal authorization; Online portal = self-service digital consent. Required by NACHA for audit trail.']
  authorization_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the EFT authorization instruction. Active = currently collecting; Suspended = temporarily halted; Cancelled = permanently terminated; Pending = awaiting pre-notification confirmation; Expired = past end date.']
  bank_routing_number varchar [note: 'Nine-digit ABA routing transit number identifying the financial institution holding the payer\'s account. Used to route ACH transactions through the Federal Reserve or EPN network.']
  billing_frequency varchar [note: 'Frequency at which premiums are collected via this EFT authorization. Aligns with the policy\'s modal billing election (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, annual). Determines the ACH debit schedule.']
  cancellation_date date [note: 'Date on which the EFT authorization was cancelled or revoked by the payer or insurer. Null if the authorization is still active. After this date no further ACH debits may be initiated under this mandate.']
  collection_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Authorized recurring debit amount in USD to be collected per billing cycle. Represents the modal premium amount including base policy premium, rider premiums, and any applicable fees authorized under this mandate.']
  collection_day varchar [note: 'Day of the month (1–28) on which recurring ACH premium debits are scheduled. Capped at 28 to avoid month-end variability. Drives the billing system\'s ACH file generation schedule.']
  consecutive_failure_count varchar [note: 'Running count of consecutive failed ACH debit attempts under this authorization. Used to trigger suspension, lapse initiation, or APL activation per the failure_handling_rule. Reset to zero upon a successful collection.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this EFT authorization record was first created in the billing system. Supports audit trail requirements under NACHA, Regulation E, and SOX.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the collection amount. Typically USD for domestic US life insurance policies. Supports multi-currency arrangements for international policyholders.']
  debit_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this authorization covers recurring periodic debits (standard modal premium collection) or a one-time debit (e.g., reinstatement payment, back-premium catch-up).']
  direct_debit_scheme varchar [note: 'Payment scheme under which this authorization operates. ACH = US Automated Clearing House (NACHA); SEPA_DD = Single Euro Payments Area Direct Debit; BACS = UK Bankers Automated Clearing Services; PAD = Canadian Pre-Authorized Debit. Determines applicable scheme rules.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date from which this EFT authorization becomes operative and the billing system may initiate ACH debits. May differ from authorization_date if a future start was requested.']
  failure_handling_rule varchar [note: 'Business rule governing how the billing system responds to a returned/failed ACH debit (NSF or other return). Retry_once/twice = re-present per NACHA rules; Suspend = suspend authorization; Lapse = initiate policy lapse process; APL_trigger = activate Automatic Premium Loan (APL) rider.']
  first_collection_date date [note: 'Date on which the first ACH debit was or is scheduled to be collected under this authorization. Used to confirm pre-notification lead time compliance and to anchor the recurring schedule.']
  instruction_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this EFT/ACH debit instruction by the billing system or originating bank. Used for reconciliation with NACHA files and bank statements.']
  kyc_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the payer\'s identity and bank account ownership have been verified per KYC/AML requirements prior to activating this EFT authorization. Required by FinCEN BSA/AML program rules.']
  kyc_verified_date date [note: 'Date on which KYC verification of the payer was completed and recorded. Used for AML compliance audit trails and periodic re-verification scheduling.']
  last_collection_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent successful ACH debit collected under this authorization. Updated after each successful collection cycle. Null if no collection has yet occurred.']
  last_failure_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent failed ACH debit return under this authorization. Used alongside last_failure_return_code for NSF tracking, grace period management, and lapse administration.']
  last_failure_return_code varchar [note: 'Most recent NACHA ACH return code received for a failed debit under this authorization (e.g., R01 = Insufficient Funds, R02 = Account Closed, R03 = No Account, R04 = Invalid Account Number, R07 = Authorization Revoked). Null if no failure has occurred.']
  mandate_reference varchar [note: 'Scheme-specific mandate reference number assigned to this authorization. For SEPA Direct Debit, this is the Unique Mandate Reference (UMR). For BACS, this is the Service User Number reference. For ACH, this maps to the instruction_reference_number.']
  masked_account_number varchar [note: 'Masked representation of the payer\'s bank account number (e.g., last 4 digits visible, remainder replaced with asterisks). Full account number is stored in a tokenized vault; this field supports display and reconciliation without exposing PCI data.']
  max_debit_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Maximum single-transaction debit amount authorized by the payer. Applicable when variable_amount_flag is True. Provides a ceiling for flexible premium collections to protect the payer from unauthorized over-debits.']
  max_retry_count varchar [note: 'Maximum number of times a failed ACH debit may be re-presented before the failure_handling_rule escalation is triggered. NACHA limits re-presentment to no more than 2 additional attempts after the original return.']
  originating_bank_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the Originating Depository Financial Institution (ODFI) as registered with the Federal Reserve or EPN. Used in NACHA file headers for ACH batch origination.']
  originating_bank_name varchar [note: 'Name of the financial institution (Originating Depository Financial Institution — ODFI) that holds the payer\'s account and through which ACH debits are originated.']
  payer_name_on_account varchar [note: 'Full legal name of the account holder as it appears on the bank account. Required for NACHA individual name field in ACH transactions and for AML/KYC verification.']
  payer_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the payer entity authorizing the EFT debit. Individual = personal policyholder; Corporate = business entity paying group premiums; Trust = ILIT or other trust arrangement; Group sponsor = employer or association paying group life premiums.']
  prenote_sent_date date [note: 'Date on which the NACHA pre-notification (zero-dollar test) was transmitted to the ODFI. The first live debit may not occur until at least 3 banking days after this date per NACHA rules.']
  prenote_status varchar [note: 'Status of the NACHA pre-notification (zero-dollar test transaction) sent to the ODFI before the first live debit. Pending = prenote initiated; Sent = prenote transmitted; Confirmed = no return received within 3 banking days; Failed = prenote returned with error.']
  sec_code varchar [note: 'NACHA Standard Entry Class code identifying the type of ACH transaction. PPD = Prearranged Payment and Deposit (personal); CCD = Corporate Credit or Debit; WEB = Internet-initiated; TEL = Telephone-initiated. Determines NACHA file formatting and return code rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PPD|CCD|WEB|TEL|ARC|BOC|POP — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational billing system from which this EFT authorization record was sourced (e.g., SAPIENS_BILLING, MAJESCO_BILLING). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver layer.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this EFT authorization record. Tracks changes to authorization status, bank details, or collection parameters for audit and compliance purposes.']
  variable_amount_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this authorization permits variable debit amounts (True) or is fixed to the collection_amount (False). Variable authorizations are used for flexible premium UL/IUL policies where the policyholder may vary premium payments.']

  Note: 'Master record of a policyholder\'s or group payer\'s electronic payment authorization for automatic recurring premium collection via EFT/ACH or direct debit. Captures bank routing number, masked account number, account type (checking/savings), authorization date, authorization method (wet signature, e-sign, voice), effective date, cancellation date, pre-notification status, instruction reference number, originating bank details, collection day, first/last collection dates, instruction status (active, suspended, cancelled), and failure handling rules. SSOT for all electronic payment mandates — both ACH debits and direct debit instructions — supporting personal and corporate payer arrangements.   premium_allocation_base decimal(18,2) [note: 'The portion of the overdue premium amount allocated to the base life insurance policy component within the Automatic Premium Loan (APL). Used for premium allocation reporting across policy components. Denominated in USD.']

  premium_allocation_riders decimal(18,2) [note: 'The portion of the overdue premium amount allocated to policy riders (e.g., ADB, LTC, waiver of premium) within the Automatic Premium Loan (APL). Riders may lapse separately if their premium component cannot be covered. Denominated in USD.']
  premium_due_date date [note: 'The original scheduled due date of the overdue premium that triggered the Automatic Premium Loan (APL). Establishes the billing cycle reference for the missed payment.']
  product_type varchar [note: 'The type of life insurance product associated with this Automatic Premium Loan (APL) transaction. APL is only applicable to Whole Life (WL) and Universal Life (UL) products that accumulate Cash Surrender Value (CSV).']
  reversal_date date [note: 'The date on which the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) was reversed, if applicable. Populated only when reversal_flag is True. Triggers reinstatement of the full Cash Surrender Value (CSV) and removal of the loan from the policy loan account.']
  reversal_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this Automatic Premium Loan (APL) transaction has been reversed. True = APL was reversed (e.g., policyholder subsequently paid the overdue premium or policy was reinstated); False = APL remains active and outstanding.']
  reversal_reason varchar [note: 'The reason code for the reversal of the Automatic Premium Loan (APL). \'premium_paid\' = policyholder paid the overdue premium after APL was posted; \'reinstatement\' = policy reinstated with back-premium payment; \'policy_surrender\' = policy surrendered and loan offset against CSV; \'system_correction\' = administrative correction; \'other\' = other reason.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the Policy Administration System instance or module that originated this Automatic Premium Loan (APL) transaction record (e.g., FAST, Sapiens LifePro, EXL). Supports data lineage and multi-system reconciliation in the lakehouse.']
  source_transaction_reference varchar [note: 'The native transaction identifier or reference number assigned by the originating Policy Administration System for this APL event. Used for reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the source system of record.']
  transaction_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible, human-readable reference number assigned to this Automatic Premium Loan (APL) transaction by the Policy Administration System. Used in policyholder correspondence, audit trails, and regulatory reporting.']
  transaction_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) transaction. \'initiated\' = APL triggered but not yet posted to policy loan account; \'posted\' = loan amount applied and premium paid; \'reversed\' = APL reversed due to subsequent premium payment or reinstatement; \'cancelled\' = APL voided before posting; \'pending_reversal\' = reversal in progress.']
  trigger_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time when the Automatic Premium Loan (APL) was triggered by the Policy Administration System, typically at the end of the grace period when the overdue premium remains unpaid. This is the principal business event timestamp for this transaction.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this Automatic Premium Loan (APL) transaction record was last modified in the data platform (Silver Layer), such as when a reversal or status update was applied. Used for change data capture and audit trail.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of an Automatic Premium Loan (APL) triggered when a policy\'s cash surrender value (CSV) is used to pay an overdue premium, preventing lapse. Captures APL trigger date, loan amount (equal to overdue premium), interest rate applied, outstanding APL balance, CSV available at trigger, and policy loan account impact. Specific to traditional whole life (WL) and universal life (UL) products with CSV. Source: Policy Administration System APL module.'

  applied_billing_period varchar [note: 'The billing period (YYYY-MM) to which the suspense payment was applied upon resolution. Used for premium reconciliation and to ensure the payment is credited to the correct modal billing cycle (annual, semi-annual, quarterly, monthly).']
  bank_account_last4 varchar [note: 'Last four digits of the bank account number from which the EFT/ACH payment was drawn. Stored in masked form for reconciliation and refund routing without retaining full account data per PCI DSS requirements.']
  check_number varchar [note: 'Check number from the remitter\'s payment instrument when the payment source type is \'check\'. Used for bank reconciliation, duplicate payment detection, and NSF (Non-Sufficient Funds) tracking.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the suspense account record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and SOX compliance requirements.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the received payment amount (e.g., USD, CAD). Required for multi-currency operations and foreign national policyholder payments.']
  customer_notification_date date [note: 'Date on which the policyholder or remitter was notified about the suspense item, requesting additional information or documentation to resolve the NIGO or unmatched payment condition.']
  days_in_suspense varchar [note: 'Number of calendar days the payment has been held in suspense since receipt_date. Drives aging bucket assignment, escalation triggers, and unclaimed property dormancy period calculations per state law.']
  dormancy_expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which the suspense item reaches the end of the applicable state unclaimed property dormancy period, after which the funds must be escheated to the state. Calculated based on receipt_date plus the state-specific dormancy period (typically 3–5 years).']
  escheatment_reference varchar [note: 'State unclaimed property filing reference number assigned when the suspense amount is transferred to a state\'s unclaimed property program. Populated when resolution_type is \'transferred_to_unclaimed\'. Required for state unclaimed property law compliance and audit.']
  escheatment_state varchar [note: 'Two-letter US state code identifying the state to which the unclaimed property was or will be escheated. Determined by the remitter\'s last known address per the priority rules established in Texas v. New Jersey (1965). Required for state unclaimed property compliance.']
  exchange_1035_reference varchar [note: 'Reference number associated with a tax-free 1035 Exchange transfer when the suspense reason is \'1035_exchange_in_transit\'. Links the suspense item to the originating carrier\'s transfer documentation. Required for IRS tax compliance under IRC Section 1035.']
  gl_suspense_account_code varchar [note: 'General Ledger (GL) account code to which the suspense amount is posted pending resolution. Required for GAAP and SAP financial reporting. Upon resolution, the amount is transferred from the GL suspense account to the appropriate premium income or liability account.']
  grace_period_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the target policy was in a grace period at the time the suspense payment was received. True = policy was in grace period; False = policy was current. Critical for lapse administration and determining urgency of suspense resolution.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to the suspense account record. Used for change tracking, reconciliation, and audit trail compliance.']
  lockbox_batch_number varchar [note: 'Bank lockbox batch identifier associated with the physical or electronic payment deposit batch in which this suspense item was received. Used for bank reconciliation and cash posting audit trail.']
  nigo_reason varchar [note: 'Specific reason the payment or accompanying documentation was classified as Not In Good Order (NIGO), when suspense_reason_code is \'nigo\'. Examples include missing policy number, incorrect payee name, unsigned check, or missing 1035 Exchange transfer form.']
  nsf_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the payment was returned by the bank due to Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF). True = NSF return received; False = no NSF. NSF payments placed in suspense require special handling including policyholder notification and potential lapse processing.']
  originating_carrier varchar [note: 'Name of the insurance carrier from which funds were transferred in a 1035 Exchange. Populated only when payment_source_type is \'1035_exchange\'. Required for IRS reporting and exchange documentation.']
  payment_method_detail varchar [note: 'Additional detail about the payment instrument, such as bank name, check number, wire reference number, or ACH trace number. Supports payment tracing and reconciliation with the bank lockbox or EFT/ACH processor.']
  payment_source_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the payment instrument or channel through which the suspense amount was received. Drives refund processing method and AML monitoring. \'1035_exchange\' indicates a tax-free policy exchange under IRC Section 1035.']
  policy_number varchar [note: 'The externally-known policy number provided by the remitter or extracted from payment documentation. May be incomplete, incorrect, or absent when the suspense reason is \'policy_not_found\'. Stored as received for audit and matching purposes.']
  premium_due_date date [note: 'The premium due date on the target policy that this suspense payment is intended to satisfy. Used to assess whether the payment, once applied, will prevent a lapse or grace period entry.']
  receipt_date date [note: 'The business date on which the unallocated or unidentified payment was received and entered into suspense. This is the principal real-world event date for the suspense item and drives aging calculations and unclaimed property dormancy periods.']
  receipt_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time the payment was received and logged into the suspense module, including timezone offset. Used for intraday reconciliation and audit trail purposes.']
  received_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Gross amount of the payment received and placed into suspense, in the currency of receipt. This is the raw amount as received before any adjustments, fees, or partial allocations.']
  remitter_name varchar [note: 'Full name of the individual or entity that submitted the payment currently held in suspense. May differ from the policyholder if payment was made by a third party, trustee, or ILIT. Required for refund processing and AML/KYC compliance.']
  resolution_date date [note: 'Business date on which the suspense item was fully or partially resolved. Null if the suspense item remains open. Used for cash reconciliation, premium posting, and audit trail.']
  resolution_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time the suspense item was resolved, including timezone offset. Supports intraday cash management and SOX audit trail requirements.']
  resolution_type varchar [note: 'Method by which the suspense item was resolved. \'applied_to_policy\' = premium applied to identified policy; \'refunded_to_sender\' = payment returned to remitter; \'transferred_to_unclaimed\' = funds transferred to state unclaimed property; \'partial_applied\' = portion applied to policy with remainder refunded or still open; \'voided\' = record cancelled due to error. Null if suspense is still open.']
  resolved_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Amount of the suspense balance that has been resolved (applied to policy, refunded, or transferred). May be less than received_amount if partial resolution occurred. Null if suspense is still open.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Native record identifier from the Sapiens BillingPro suspense module. Enables lineage tracing back to the operational system of record for reconciliation and data quality validation in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  suspense_reason_code varchar [note: 'Coded reason explaining why the payment was placed into suspense rather than applied directly to a policy. \'policy_not_found\' = no matching policy located; \'nigo\' = Not In Good Order (NIGO) — missing or incorrect documentation; \'amount_mismatch\' = payment does not match expected premium; \'1035_exchange_in_transit\' = tax-free 1035 Exchange funds awaiting policy setup; \'duplicate_payment\' = potential duplicate of an existing payment; \'unidentified_remitter\' = payer cannot be identified; \'currency_mismatch\' = payment currency does not match policy currency. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: policy_not_found|nigo|amount_mismatch|1035_exchange_in_transit|duplicate_payment|unidentified_remitter|currency_mismatch — promote to reference product]']
  suspense_reason_description varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative providing additional detail about why the payment was placed in suspense. Supplements the suspense_reason_code with case-specific context entered by the billing operations team.']
  suspense_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible, human-readable reference number assigned to the suspense item at receipt. Used in correspondence with policyholders, agents, and remitters to track unallocated payments. Format: SUS-YYYY-NNNNNNNN.']
  suspense_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the suspense item. \'open\' = unresolved and pending action; \'resolved\' = successfully applied to a policy; \'refunded\' = returned to remitter; \'transferred_to_unclaimed\' = moved to state unclaimed property; \'escheatment_pending\' = awaiting formal escheatment filing; \'voided\' = cancelled due to error or duplicate.']
  unresolved_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Remaining balance of the suspense item that has not yet been resolved. Equals received_amount minus resolved_amount. Used for open-item reconciliation and cash management reporting under GAAP/SAP.']

  Note: 'Master and transactional record tracking unallocated or unidentified premium payments held in suspense, from creation through resolution. Captures suspense receipt date, amount, payment source, reason for suspense (policy not found, NIGO, amount mismatch, 1035 exchange in transit), aging bucket, resolution status, resolution date, resolution type (applied to policy, refunded to sender, transferred to unclaimed property), resolved amount, resolving user, target policy, and escheatment reference. Provides full audit trail for suspense creation through clearance. Critical for premium reconciliation, GAAP/SAP cash management, and state unclaimed property law compliance. Source: Sapiens BillingPro suspense module.'
}

Distinct from the policyholder — supports list billing, payroll deduction, and government allotment scenarios.']
  primary_plan_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to product.product_plan. Business justification: Multi-policy billing accounts benefit from tracking the primary/dominant product for portfolio analysis, cross-sell targeting, customer segmentation, and account-level service strategies. Enables prod']

Active indicates premiums are being collected normally; suspended indicates a temporary hold (e.g., grace period); lapsed indicates the account has passed the grace period without payment; closed indicates the account is permanently terminated; pending indicates setup in progress; reinstated indicates a previously lapsed account restored to active status.']
  account_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the billing arrangement governing how premiums are collected. Direct bill sends invoices to the individual payer; list bill aggregates multiple policies under an employer or group sponsor; payroll deduction routes premiums through employer payroll; government allotment routes through federal/state benefit programs; EFT/ACH and bank draft indicate electronic collection methods at the account level.']

  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this billing account record was first created in the source system. Supports audit trail requirements, SOX compliance, and data lineage tracking in the lakehouse silver layer.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this billing account (e.g., USD). Supports multi-currency payer scenarios for international life insurance products.']
  delinquency_indicator boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether this billing account is currently delinquent — i.e., a premium payment is past due and the account is within or beyond the grace period. True indicates delinquent status requiring collection action or lapse processing.']

  eft_authorization_date date [note: 'The date on which the payer authorized Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT)/ACH debit for premium collection. Required for NACHA compliance to evidence pre-authorization of recurring ACH debits. Null for non-EFT payment methods.']
  grace_period_end_date date [note: 'The date on which the grace period expires for the current unpaid billing cycle. After this date, policies under the account are subject to lapse per state-mandated grace period rules (typically 30 days for life insurance, 61 days for some products). Null when account is current.']
  kyc_verified_indicator boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the payer has completed Know Your Customer (KYC) identity verification as required by AML/BSA regulations. True indicates verification is complete and on file. Required for FinCEN compliance and AML program adherence.']
  last_nsf_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) or returned payment event on this billing account. Used alongside NSF count to assess payment reliability and trigger EFT suspension rules.']
  last_payment_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The monetary amount of the most recent premium payment received on this billing account. Used for reconciliation, delinquency analysis, and partial payment tracking.']
  last_payment_date date [note: 'The date on which the most recent premium payment was successfully received and applied to this billing account. Used for delinquency monitoring, grace period calculation, and lapse administration.']
  next_due_date date [note: 'The date on which the next premium payment is due for this billing account based on the billing frequency and last payment date. Drives billing notice generation and grace period monitoring.']
  nsf_count varchar [note: 'Cumulative count of Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) or returned payment events on this billing account. Used for payment risk scoring, EFT eligibility assessment, and potential account suspension decisions.']
  paperless_billing_indicator boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the payer has opted into paperless (electronic-only) billing and statement delivery, suppressing physical mail generation. Supports green initiative tracking and operational cost reduction.']
  payment_method varchar [note: 'The preferred payment instrument used to remit premiums for this billing account. ACH/EFT indicates electronic funds transfer from a bank account; check indicates paper check; credit card indicates card-based payment; wire transfer indicates bank wire; payroll deduction and government allotment indicate employer or agency-routed collection.']
  policy_count varchar [note: 'Number of active insurance policies currently aggregated under this billing account. Supports list billing administration and account-level premium aggregation reporting.']
  reinstatement_date date [note: 'The date on which a previously lapsed billing account was reinstated following satisfaction of reinstatement requirements (e.g., payment of back premiums, evidence of insurability). Null for accounts that have never lapsed or have not been reinstated.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational source system from which this billing account record was ingested (e.g., SAPIENS_BILLING, MAJESCO_BILLING, FAST_BILLING). Supports data lineage tracking and multi-system reconciliation in the lakehouse.']
  termination_date date [note: 'The date on which this billing account was permanently closed or terminated. Null for accounts that remain active or suspended. Populated upon account closure, policy lapse beyond reinstatement window, or group contract termination.']
  total_billed_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total premium amount currently billed and outstanding on this billing account for the current billing cycle, covering all policies and riders under the account. Represents the gross amount due before any credits or adjustments.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this billing account record was most recently modified in the source system. Used for incremental ETL processing, change data capture, and audit trail maintenance.']

  Note: 'Master record representing the billing relationship entity that aggregates one or more policies under a single payer arrangement. Supports list billing (employer/group), direct bill, payroll deduction, and government allotment scenarios. Captures payer identity, billing address, payment method preference, billing frequency, account balance, account status (active, suspended, closed), last payment date, and delinquency indicator. Distinct from the policyholder identity (owned by policyholder domain) — this is the financial billing relationship. SSOT for the payer-level billing aggregation point.'
}

Required for rate compliance verification, audit trail, and ensuring adjustments match approved rate']
  report_period_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to reporting.report_period. Business justification: Premium adjustments (rate changes, corrections, COLA increases) must be allocated to the correct reporting period for accurate revenue recognition, premium income reporting, and GAAP/statutory reconci']
  reversed_adjustment_premium_adjustment_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the original premium_adjustment_id that this record reverses, when reversal_indicator is True. Enables bidirectional audit trail linking between original and reversal adjustment records.']
  adjustment_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The net monetary change in modal premium resulting from this adjustment (new_modal_premium minus prior_modal_premium). A positive value indicates a premium increase; a negative value indicates a decrease. Used for financial reporting and actuarial analysis.']
  adjustment_number varchar [note: 'Externally visible, human-readable business identifier for this premium adjustment transaction, assigned by the Policy Administration System or Billing System (e.g., ADJ-2024-00123456). Used for audit trail, correspondence, and reconciliation.']
  adjustment_reason_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code identifying the business reason for the premium adjustment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ANNIV_RATE_CHG|ATTAINED_AGE|RIDER_ADD|RIDER_REMOVE|FACE_AMT_CHG|RISK_RECLASS|COLA|REG_RATE_REV|UW_REVISION|BILLING_CORR — promote to reference product]']
  adjustment_reason_description varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative description of the reason for the premium adjustment, providing additional context beyond the standardized reason code. May include details such as the specific rider added, the new risk class assigned, or the regulatory revision reference.']
  adjustment_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow lifecycle state of the premium adjustment record. \'pending\' indicates awaiting approval; \'approved\' indicates authorized but not yet applied to billing; \'applied\' indicates posted to the billing schedule; \'reversed\' indicates a previously applied adjustment that has been backed out; \'rejected\' indicates the adjustment was denied.']
  adjustment_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the direction and nature of the premium adjustment. \'increase\' indicates the new premium is higher than the prior; \'decrease\' indicates the new premium is lower; \'correction\' indicates a billing error fix with no net change in intended premium; \'reversal\' indicates the cancellation of a previously applied adjustment.']
  approval_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this premium adjustment required and received formal authorization. \'not_required\' for system-generated adjustments within automated rules; \'pending\' for adjustments awaiting human review; \'approved\' for authorized adjustments; \'rejected\' for denied adjustments. Supports SOX and market conduct compliance.']
  approval_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this premium adjustment was formally approved by the authorizing user or automated system. Null when approval_status is \'not_required\' or \'pending\'. Supports SOX audit trail and turnaround time reporting.']
  approved_by varchar [note: 'The user ID or system identifier of the individual or automated process that approved this premium adjustment. Null when approval_status is \'not_required\'. Required for SOX audit trail on manual or exception adjustments.']
  attained_age varchar [note: 'The insured\'s attained age (in whole years) at the time of this premium adjustment. Relevant for attained-age recalculation adjustments on Yearly Renewable Term (YRT), Universal Life (UL), and Indexed Universal Life (IUL) products where COI rates are age-banded.']
  billing_mode varchar [note: 'The modal billing frequency of the policy at the time of this adjustment (annual, semi-annual, quarterly, or monthly). Determines the modal factor applied to convert annual premium to the scheduled payment amount.']
  cola_rate decimal(7,4) [note: 'The Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) percentage rate applied to the premium when the adjustment_reason_code is COLA. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0300 for 3%). Null for non-COLA adjustments.']
  component_type varchar [note: 'Identifies the specific premium component affected by this adjustment: \'base\' for the base policy premium, \'rider\' for a policy rider premium, \'coi\' for Cost of Insurance (COI) charges on universal life products, or \'apl\' for Automatic Premium Loan (APL) repayment component.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this premium adjustment record (e.g., USD). Supports multi-currency policy administration for international or expatriate life insurance products.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the premium adjustment becomes effective on the policy billing schedule. This is the business event date — the date from which the new premium amount applies, which may differ from the transaction processing date.']
  mec_test_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this premium adjustment triggered a Modified Endowment Contract (MEC) test review under IRC Section 7702A. True when the adjustment requires validation that the new premium level does not cause the policy to fail the 7-pay test and become classified as a MEC.']
  new_annual_premium decimal(18,2) [note: 'The annualized premium amount (Annual Premium Equivalent) that will apply after this adjustment, calculated by annualizing the new modal premium based on the billing mode. Supports APE reporting, actuarial reserving, and regulatory filings.']
  new_face_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The policy face amount (death benefit) that applies after this adjustment. Captured when the adjustment is triggered by a face amount change. Used to verify 7702 compliance and recalculate guideline premium limits.']
  new_modal_premium decimal(18,2) [note: 'The modal premium amount (per billing frequency) that will apply to the policy billing schedule after this adjustment is applied. This becomes the new scheduled premium for future billing cycles.']
  new_risk_class varchar [note: 'The underwriting risk classification assigned to the insured after this adjustment (e.g., Preferred Plus, Preferred, Standard, Substandard, Table-rated). Captured when adjustment_reason_code indicates a risk class reclassification event.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional operational notes, exception handling comments, or supplementary context recorded by the billing operations team regarding this premium adjustment. Not used for structured data; intended for human-readable commentary.']
  policy_year varchar [note: 'The policy year (1-based count from policy issue date) in which this premium adjustment is effective. Used for anniversary-based rate change processing, attained age recalculations, and actuarial experience studies.']
  prior_annual_premium decimal(18,2) [note: 'The annualized premium amount (Annual Premium Equivalent) in effect before this adjustment, calculated by annualizing the prior modal premium based on the billing mode. Supports APE reporting and actuarial valuation.']
  prior_face_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The policy face amount (death benefit) in effect before this adjustment. Captured when the adjustment is triggered by a face amount change, as face amount directly drives base premium calculations.']
  prior_modal_premium decimal(18,2) [note: 'The modal premium amount (per billing frequency) in effect on the policy billing schedule immediately before this adjustment was applied. Provides the baseline for calculating the adjustment delta and supports audit trail requirements.']
  prior_risk_class varchar [note: 'The underwriting risk classification assigned to the insured before this adjustment (e.g., Preferred Plus, Preferred, Standard, Substandard, Table-rated). Captured when adjustment_reason_code indicates a risk class reclassification event.']
  processed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the premium adjustment was fully processed and posted to the billing schedule in the Policy Administration or Billing System. Supports audit trail and SLA monitoring for billing operations.']
  product_code varchar [note: 'The internal product code identifying the life insurance or annuity product type associated with the policy (e.g., WL, UL, IUL, VUL, YRT, SPIA, FIA). Supports product-level premium adjustment analytics and actuarial segmentation.']
  regulatory_revision_ref varchar [note: 'Reference identifier for the regulatory filing, state department of insurance bulletin, or NAIC model regulation revision that mandated this premium rate adjustment. Populated when adjustment_reason_code is REG_RATE_REV. Supports regulatory compliance audit trail.']
  reversal_indicator boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether this adjustment record is a reversal of a previously applied adjustment. True when this record cancels and backs out a prior adjustment; False for original adjustments. Used in financial reconciliation to net out reversed transactions.']
  rider_code varchar [note: 'The standardized code identifying the specific policy rider whose premium is being adjusted, when the component_type is \'rider\'. Examples include ADB (Accidental Death Benefit), AWL (Automatic Waiver of Premium), LTC (Long-Term Care), or DI (Disability Income) riders. Null when adjustment applies to base premium or COI.']
  seven_pay_premium decimal(18,2) [note: 'The maximum annual premium allowed under the IRC Section 7702A seven-pay test at the time of this adjustment. Captured when mec_test_flag is True to document the compliance threshold against which the new premium was evaluated.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record that originated this premium adjustment transaction. \'PAS\' = Policy Administration System (e.g., Sapiens LifePro, FAST); \'BILLING\' = Billing and Premium Collection System (e.g., Sapiens BillingPro); \'UW_WORKBENCH\' = Underwriting Workbench; \'ACTUARIAL\' = Actuarial Valuation System; \'MANUAL\' = manual override by authorized user.']
  source_transaction_reference varchar [note: 'The transaction identifier from the originating source system (Policy Administration System or Billing System) that authorized and triggered this premium adjustment. Provides end-to-end traceability from the billing data product back to the system of record.']
  state_of_issue varchar [note: 'The two-letter US state code of the state in which the policy was issued. Determines the applicable state insurance regulations, rate filing requirements, and consumer protection rules governing this premium adjustment.']
  transaction_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the premium adjustment transaction was created and recorded in the source system. Represents the system-of-record capture time, distinct from the business effective date.']

  Note: 'Transactional record of premium adjustments applied to a policy\'s billing schedule, including rate changes due to policy anniversary, attained age recalculation, rider addition or removal, face amount change, risk class reclassification, cost of living adjustment (COLA), or regulatory rate revision. Captures adjustment effective date, prior premium amount, new premium amount, adjustment reason code, authorizing source system transaction, and approval status. Provides audit trail for all premium amount changes on the billing schedule.'
}

  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the transaction record was first created in the system.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code indicating the currency in which the transaction was denominated.']
  customer_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the customer who is the party to this transaction.']
  description varchar [note: 'Free-text description providing additional context or details about the transaction.']
  due_date date [note: 'The date by which payment for this transaction is expected or required.']
  exchange_rate decimal(12,6) [note: 'The foreign exchange rate applied if the transaction involved currency conversion.']
  fee_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Any processing fees, service charges, or administrative fees associated with the transaction.']

  nsf_indicator boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the transaction failed due to non-sufficient funds in the payment account.']

  payment_method varchar [note: 'The financial instrument or mechanism used to execute the transaction.']
  policy_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the policy associated with this transaction.']
  posting_date date [note: 'The accounting date on which the transaction was posted to the general ledger.']
  processed_by_user_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the user or agent who processed or approved the transaction.']
  reconciliation_date date [note: 'The date on which the transaction was reconciled with external financial records.']
  reconciliation_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the transaction has been reconciled with bank statements and financial records.']
  reinstatement_indicator boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether this transaction is part of a policy reinstatement process following a lapse.']
  reversal_indicator boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether this transaction is a reversal of a previous transaction.']
  reversed_transaction_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the original transaction that this transaction reverses, if applicable.']
  tax_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total tax amount applied to the transaction, including premium tax and other applicable taxes.']
  transaction_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The gross monetary value of the transaction before any adjustments or fees.']
  transaction_category varchar [note: 'High-level grouping of transaction types for reporting and analytics.']
  transaction_date date [note: 'The business date on which the transaction occurred or was effective.']
  transaction_number varchar [note: 'Externally-visible unique transaction number used for customer communication and reconciliation.']
  transaction_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the transaction indicating its processing status.']
  transaction_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the transaction was executed or recorded in the system.']
  transaction_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the transaction indicating its business purpose within the billing domain.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the transaction record was last modified.']
  value_date date [note: 'The date from which the transaction amount becomes effective for interest calculation or valuation purposes.']

  Note: 'Master reference table for transaction. Referenced by transaction_id.'
}

  rmd_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this contract is subject to IRS Required Minimum Distribution (RMD) rules.   suitability_review_status varchar [note: 'The status of the annuity suitability review conducted at point of sale per NAIC Annuity Suitability Model Regulation #275 and the DOL Best Interest Standard.   surrender_charge_period_years varchar [note: 'The total number of contract years during which surrender charges apply, as defined by the product\'s surrender charge schedule (e.g., 7-year, 10-year surrender charge period).   tax_qualification_status varchar [note: 'Indicates the tax qualification status of the annuity contract under IRS rules.   updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this annuity contract record was last modified in the lakehouse silver layer, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).   Note: 'Master record for each annuity contract issued by the company, serving as the SSOT for all annuity contract administration.
