  is_retrocession boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this cession is a retrocession arrangement (i.e., the cedant is itself a reinsurer ceding risk to a retrocessionaire). True for retrocession cessions; False for direct cessions from a primary insurer. Used to distinguish retrocession layers in NAIC Schedule S Part 6.']
  modco_reserve_adjustment decimal(18,2) [note: 'The reserve adjustment amount payable under a modified coinsurance arrangement, representing the change in the reinsurer\'s notional reserve share held by the cedant, expressed in USD. Applicable only when is_modified_coinsurance is True. Required for NAIC Schedule S Part 4 and statutory reserve reporting.']
  nar decimal(18,2) [note: 'The Net Amount at Risk (NAR) ceded to the reinsurer as of the valuation date, expressed in USD. For YRT treaties, NAR equals the ceded death benefit minus the policy reserve. NAR is the primary basis for YRT reinsurance premium calculation and RBC C-1 credit risk exposure measurement.']
  policy_issue_date date [note: 'The date the underlying life insurance policy was issued by the cedant. Used to determine policy duration, YRT rate band applicability, and treaty vintage for actuarial experience studies and ceded block segmentation.']
  policy_number varchar [note: 'The externally-known policy identifier from the Policy Administration System (e.g., FAST, Sapiens LifePro). Included directly on the snapshot for bordereaux reporting and reinsurer reconciliation without requiring a join to the policy master.']
  rbc_credit_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The Risk-Based Capital (RBC) credit attributable to this cession as of the valuation date, expressed in USD. Represents the reduction in C-1 credit risk capital requirement resulting from the reinsurance arrangement. Used in RBC C-1 calculations and ORSA reporting.']
  reinsurance_basis varchar [note: 'The age basis used for calculating YRT reinsurance premiums. Attained age uses the insured\'s current age each year; original age uses the age at policy issue; issue age uses the age at cession inception. Determines the YRT rate table lookup methodology.']
  reinsurer_authorization_status varchar [note: 'The authorization status of the reinsurer in the cedant\'s state of domicile as of the valuation date. Authorized reinsurers allow full reserve credit; unauthorized reinsurers require collateral (letters of credit or trust funds). Critical for NAIC Schedule S Part 3 and reserve credit eligibility.']
  reinsurer_naic_code varchar [note: 'The five-digit NAIC company code assigned to the reinsurer. Required for NAIC Schedule S statutory filing to identify the assuming reinsurer. Used for reinsurer credit quality assessment and RBC counterparty risk reporting.']
  retained_face_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The portion of the total policy face amount retained by the cedant (direct writer) after cession, expressed in USD. Retained amount equals total face amount minus ceded face amount. Required for retention limit compliance monitoring and NAIC Schedule S reporting.']
  retention_limit decimal(18,2) [note: 'The maximum face amount the cedant retains on any single life under the applicable treaty or company retention schedule, expressed in USD. Used to validate that ceded amounts comply with treaty automatic binding limits and company retention policy.']
  risk_class varchar [note: 'The underwriting risk classification assigned to the insured at policy issue, as determined by the Underwriting Workbench (e.g., RGAX AURA, Swiss Re Magnum). Drives YRT reinsurance premium rates and NAR-based cession calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: preferred_plus|preferred|standard_plus|standard|substandard|rated|uninsurable — promote to reference product]']
  schedule_s_part varchar [note: 'The NAIC Schedule S part to which this cession snapshot record contributes. Part 1: Ceded reinsurance; Part 2: Assumed reinsurance; Part 3: Reinsurer details; Part 4: Reserve credits; Part 5: Terminated cessions; Part 6: Retrocessions. Used for statutory filing preparation.']
  smoker_status varchar [note: 'The tobacco/smoker classification of the insured as determined at underwriting. Drives YRT reinsurance premium rate selection and mortality risk segmentation. Required for actuarial experience studies and ceded block analysis.']
  snapshot_run_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the snapshot extraction process was executed. May differ from valuation_date in cases of late runs, restatements, or retroactive adjustments. Used for lineage and audit trail purposes.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this cession snapshot record was last modified in the silver layer. For immutable snapshot records, this is typically set only on initial load; updates indicate restatements or corrections. Used for audit trail and data quality monitoring.']
  valuation_date date [note: 'The period-end date as of which this cession snapshot was captured. Represents the immutable point-in-time reference for all financial and risk values in this record. Primary key for snapshot partitioning and NAIC Schedule S statutory reporting periods.']
  yrt_rate_per_thousand decimal(10,6) [note: 'The YRT reinsurance premium rate per $1,000 of Net Amount at Risk (NAR) applicable to this cession as of the valuation date. Sourced from the treaty rate schedule based on insured age, gender, risk class, and smoker status. Used to validate ceded premium calculations.']

  Note: 'Periodic point-in-time snapshot of all active cessions capturing the in-force ceded block as of a valuation date. Stores ceded face amount, NAR, reinsurance reserve credit, ceded premium, plan code, risk class, treaty reference, and reinsurer per cession as of the snapshot date. Primary data source for NAIC Schedule S statutory reporting (Parts 1-6), actuarial ceded reserve valuation, RBC C-1 credit risk calculations, and reinsurance block reconciliation. Distinct from the live cession record — this is the immutable historical valuation record used for period-end reporting.'
}

  age_band_max varchar [note: 'The maximum attained age (inclusive) of the insured for which this automatic binding limit row applies. Together with age_band_min, defines the age band dimension of the cession routing matrix.']
  age_band_min varchar [note: 'The minimum attained age (inclusive) of the insured for which this automatic binding limit row applies. Age banding is a standard actuarial practice in reinsurance treaty design as mortality risk and NAR vary significantly by age.']
  amendment_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the business reason for creating or amending this binding limit record (e.g., treaty renegotiation, capacity adjustment, regulatory change, experience-driven repricing). Supports audit trail and governance review.']
  approval_date date [note: 'The date on which this binding limit record was formally approved by the authorized approver. Supports governance audit trail and SOX compliance documentation.']
  automatic_capacity_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total aggregate face amount capacity available under the automatic treaty for new cessions. Once this capacity is exhausted, new risks must be submitted facultatively even if they fall within the per-policy binding limit. Null indicates unlimited capacity.']
  binding_limit_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The maximum face amount (death benefit) in the treaty currency that can be automatically ceded to the reinsurer under this treaty without requiring facultative submission. Risks with face amounts at or below this threshold qualify for automatic placement. This is the principal quantitative fact of this reference record.']
  cession_basis varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this limit record governs automatic cessions, facultative cessions, or an automatic-facultative arrangement. Drives the cession routing logic in the Reinsurance Management System to determine placement pathway.']
  cession_percentage decimal(7,4) [note: 'The percentage of the eligible risk (face amount or NAR) that is ceded to the reinsurer under quota-share or coinsurance arrangements. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.9000 = 90%). Applicable primarily for coinsurance and quota-share treaty types; may be null for YRT treaties where cession is based on NAR excess over retention.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this automatic binding limit record was first created in the data platform. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the binding limit and jumbo limit amounts are denominated (e.g., USD, CAD). Required for multi-currency treaty arrangements with international reinsurers such as Swiss Re or RGA.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this automatic binding limit record becomes operative for cession routing decisions. New business applications with policy effective dates on or after this date are subject to this limit.']
  facultative_threshold_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The face amount above the automatic binding limit at which the ceding company must submit the risk facultatively to the reinsurer. Risks between the binding limit and this threshold may be eligible for automatic-facultative placement; risks above this threshold require full facultative submission.']
  flat_extra_max decimal(10,2) [note: 'The maximum flat extra premium per thousand of face amount (per mille) that is eligible for automatic cession under this binding limit. Risks with flat extras exceeding this threshold require facultative submission. Null indicates no flat extra restriction.']
  insured_gender varchar [note: 'The gender of the insured to which this binding limit applies. Some treaties define gender-specific binding limits due to mortality differentials. A value of Unisex indicates the limit applies regardless of gender.']
  is_aviation_excluded boolean [note: 'Indicates whether risks involving aviation hazards (private pilot, commercial pilot, or frequent flyer exclusions) are excluded from automatic cession eligibility under this binding limit. When True, aviation-rated risks must be submitted facultatively.']
  is_foreign_national_excluded boolean [note: 'Indicates whether foreign nationals (non-US citizens or non-permanent residents) are excluded from automatic cession eligibility under this binding limit. When True, policies on foreign nationals must be submitted facultatively regardless of face amount.']
  is_jumbo_check_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a jumbo limit check (aggregate in-force across all reinsurers on the same life) must be performed before automatic cession is permitted under this binding limit. When True, the cession routing system must query total in-force amounts across all treaties before confirming automatic placement.']
  is_mib_check_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a Medical Information Bureau (MIB) check is required as a condition of automatic cession eligibility under this binding limit. When True, the underwriting workbench must confirm MIB clearance before the risk qualifies for automatic placement.']
  issue_age_basis varchar [note: 'The age calculation convention used to determine the insured\'s age for applying the age band (e.g., Age Last Birthday, Age Nearest Birthday). Must align with the age basis used in the Policy Administration System to ensure consistent cession routing.']
  jumbo_limit_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The maximum total in-force amount across all reinsurers on a single life (aggregate across all treaties) beyond which the risk is considered a jumbo risk and requires special handling or facultative placement regardless of individual treaty binding limits. Prevents over-concentration of risk on a single life.']
  limit_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this automatic binding limit record. Active records are used in cession routing. Superseded records have been replaced by a newer version. Expired records are past their termination date. Suspended records are temporarily inactive pending treaty renegotiation.']
  nar_basis varchar [note: 'Specifies whether the binding limit is applied against the full face amount (death benefit) or the Net Amount at Risk (NAR), which is the death benefit less the policy reserve or account value. NAR-based limits are common in UL and IUL products where the NAR decreases as the account value grows.']
  reinsurer_treaty_reference varchar [note: 'The reinsurer\'s own internal reference number or identifier for this treaty and binding limit schedule. Used for reconciliation with reinsurer bordereaux reports and correspondence from partners such as RGA or Swiss Re.']
  retention_limit_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The maximum face amount the ceding company retains on its own books before ceding the excess to the reinsurer under this treaty. Used in conjunction with the binding limit to determine the ceded portion (face amount minus retention). Supports NAR-based cession calculations.']
  risk_class varchar [note: 'The underwriting risk classification for which this binding limit applies (e.g., Preferred Plus, Preferred, Standard, Substandard). Automatic binding limits typically vary by risk class as higher-risk classifications may have lower automatic limits or require facultative submission.']
  smoker_status varchar [note: 'The tobacco/smoker classification of the insured to which this binding limit applies. Smoker and non-smoker populations carry different mortality rates and may have distinct binding limits under the treaty.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational source system from which this binding limit record was extracted (e.g., SWISS_RE_IRIS, RGA_AURA, INTERNAL_TREATY_MGMT). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  source_system_limit_ref varchar [note: 'The natural key or record identifier assigned to this binding limit record in the originating source system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS internal limit ID or RGA AURA schedule reference). Enables reconciliation between the Silver Layer and the source system.']
  state_code varchar [note: 'Two-letter US state code (USPS abbreviation) for which this binding limit applies, if the limit is state-specific. Null indicates the limit applies in all states. Some states have regulatory restrictions that may affect automatic binding limits.']
  table_rating_max varchar [note: 'The maximum substandard table rating (e.g., Table A through Table P, or Table 1 through Table 16) eligible for automatic cession under this binding limit. Risks with table ratings exceeding this threshold must be submitted facultatively. Null indicates no table rating restriction.']
  termination_date date [note: 'The date on which this automatic binding limit record ceases to be operative. Null indicates the record is currently active with no defined end date. Used to support historical versioning of binding limits as treaties are amended.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this automatic binding limit record was last modified in the data platform. Used to detect changes and support incremental processing in the Databricks Silver Layer ETL pipeline.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Sequential version number for this binding limit record within the same treaty/plan/risk-class/age-band combination. Incremented each time the binding limit is amended. Supports historical audit trail and point-in-time cession routing reconstruction.']

  Note: 'Reference table defining the automatic binding limits per treaty, plan code, risk class, and age band — the maximum face amount that can be automatically ceded without facultative submission. Captures treaty reference, plan code, risk class, age band, automatic binding limit amount, jumbo limit, and effective date. Drives the cession routing logic determining whether a risk qualifies for automatic or facultative placement.'
}

Table reinsurance.retention_limit {
  retention_limit_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each retention limit record. Primary key for the retention_limit reference table. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE — this is a reference/configuration record defining net retention and automatic binding limit thresholds used in cession routing decisions.']
  plan_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to product.product_plan. Business justification: Retention limits vary by product plan. Required for cession amount calculation, treaty compliance validation, and retention strategy management. Plan_code and product_line are denormalized; FK enables']
  pricing_basis_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to actuarial.pricing_basis. Business justification: Retention limits are established using pricing bases and profitability targets to optimize risk retention vs reinsurance cost. Essential for retention strategy and treaty design.']
  prior_limit_retention_limit_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the immediately preceding version of this retention limit record that was superseded. Enables a linked history chain for audit trail and regulatory review of limit changes over time.']
  reinsurance_treaty_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the reinsurance treaty under which this retention or automatic binding limit applies. Links the limit record to the governing treaty agreement with the reinsurer (e.g., RGA, Swiss Re).']
  reinsurer_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the reinsurance counterparty (e.g., RGA, Swiss Re, Munich Re) for whom this automatic binding limit or retention schedule applies. Some treaties involve multiple reinsurers with different binding limits per reinsurer.']
  age_band_max varchar [note: 'The maximum attained age (inclusive) of the insured for which this retention limit record applies. Combined with age_band_min to define the age band. Null indicates no upper age restriction for this limit record.']
  age_band_min varchar [note: 'The minimum attained age (inclusive) of the insured for which this retention limit record applies. Combined with age_band_max to define the age band. Retention and automatic binding limits typically vary by age due to increasing mortality risk at older ages.']
  approval_date date [note: 'The date on which this retention limit record was formally approved by the authorized actuarial or reinsurance management authority. Required for SOX compliance and internal governance documentation of limit changes.']
  approved_by varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the individual (typically Chief Actuary, VP Reinsurance, or CRO) who authorized this retention limit record. Supports governance, audit trail, and SOX internal control requirements.']
  cession_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this limit record governs automatic cessions (risks ceded within treaty terms without individual submission), facultative cessions (risks requiring individual reinsurer approval), or facultative-obligatory arrangements. Automatic binding limits apply only to automatic cession type.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this retention limit record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX compliance requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  credit_for_reinsurance_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the reinsurer qualifies for credit for reinsurance under applicable state insurance law, allowing the ceding company to take a reserve credit on its statutory balance sheet. Determined by reinsurer licensure status and collateral arrangements.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the limit amount is denominated (e.g., USD). Required for multi-currency treaty arrangements and international reinsurance partners.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this retention or binding limit record becomes operative and governs cession routing decisions. Aligns with treaty effective dates and policy year boundaries.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this retention or binding limit record ceases to be operative. Null indicates an open-ended limit with no scheduled expiration. Used in conjunction with effective_date to determine the applicable limit for a given valuation or cession date.']
  flat_extra_max decimal(10,2) [note: 'The maximum flat extra premium per thousand of face amount (expressed in dollars per thousand) eligible for automatic cession under this limit. Risks with flat extras exceeding this threshold require facultative submission. Null indicates no flat extra restriction.']
  gender varchar [note: 'Gender classification band to which this retention limit applies. Some treaty structures differentiate retention limits by gender due to mortality table differences. Unisex indicates the limit applies to all genders. Null indicates no gender restriction.']
  jumbo_limit_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The absolute maximum face amount threshold above which facultative reinsurance submission is required, regardless of whether the risk falls within the automatic binding limit. Risks exceeding the jumbo limit cannot be automatically ceded and must be individually underwritten by the reinsurer. Null if this record is not of type jumbo_limit.']
  limit_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The principal monetary threshold value for this limit record, expressed in the applicable currency. For retention_per_life and retention_per_policy, this is the maximum net face amount retained by the company. For automatic_binding_limit, this is the maximum face amount that can be auto-ceded. For jumbo_limit, this is the threshold above which facultative submission is mandatory. Drives the cession routing decision engine.']
  limit_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this retention or binding limit configuration within the reinsurance management system (e.g., RET-WL-NS-M-01). Used as the business key for cross-system reference and bordereaux reporting.']
  limit_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description providing additional context about this retention limit record, including any special conditions, exceptions, or treaty-specific notes that are not captured in structured fields. Used by reinsurance analysts and actuaries for reference.']
  limit_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the retention limit record. Active records drive live cession routing decisions. Superseded records have been replaced by a newer version. Expired records are past their effective period. Pending records are approved but not yet in effect.']
  limit_type varchar [note: 'Classifies the nature of the limit record: retention_per_life (maximum net amount retained across all policies on a single life), retention_per_policy (maximum net amount retained on a single policy), automatic_binding_limit (maximum face amount that can be automatically ceded without facultative submission), or jumbo_limit (threshold above which facultative reinsurance submission is required regardless of treaty).']
  nar_basis varchar [note: 'Specifies the basis on which the retention limit amount is measured: face_amount (total death benefit face), NAR (Net Amount at Risk — death benefit minus reserve), account_value (for UL/IUL/FIA products), or death_benefit (total contractual death benefit including riders). Drives the NAR-based cession calculation methodology.']
  per_life_limit_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The maximum total net amount the company will retain across all policies insuring the same life (insured). When total in-force exposure on a single life exceeds this threshold, the excess must be ceded. Critical for managing concentration risk on high-value lives.']
  policy_year_max varchar [note: 'The maximum policy year (inclusive) for which this retention limit applies. Null indicates the limit applies through the end of the policy term. Used in conjunction with policy_year_min to define the policy year band.']
  policy_year_min varchar [note: 'The minimum policy year (inclusive) for which this retention limit applies. Some treaties define different retention schedules for early policy years versus later years, particularly for YRT (Yearly Renewable Term) treaties where NAR changes over time.']
  rate_table_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the actuarial rate table used to derive the retention limit amounts (e.g., 2017CSO, 2001CSO, company-specific mortality table). Ensures traceability between limit values and the underlying actuarial assumptions used in their derivation.']
  rbc_credit_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether cessions made under this retention limit qualify for RBC (Risk-Based Capital) credit under NAIC RBC formula requirements. RBC-eligible cessions reduce the company\'s required capital, making this flag critical for capital optimization and ORSA reporting.']
  risk_class varchar [note: 'Underwriting risk classification band to which this retention limit applies. Retention limits and automatic binding limits typically vary by risk class, as higher-risk classifications carry greater mortality exposure. Null indicates the limit applies across all risk classes.']
  smoker_status varchar [note: 'Tobacco use classification band to which this retention limit applies. Smoker and non-smoker populations carry materially different mortality rates, often resulting in distinct retention schedules. Null indicates the limit applies regardless of smoker status.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational system of record from which this retention limit record originated (e.g., SWISS_RE_IRIS, RGA_AURA, INTERNAL_TREATY_MGR). Supports data lineage tracking and ETL reconciliation in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.']
  source_system_limit_ref varchar [note: 'The native identifier or reference number assigned to this retention limit record in the originating operational system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS internal limit ID). Enables cross-system reconciliation and traceability from the silver layer back to the source system.']
  state_code varchar [note: 'Two-letter US state code indicating the jurisdiction to which this retention limit applies. Some state departments of insurance impose specific retention requirements or restrict automatic binding limits. Null indicates the limit applies across all states.']
  table_rating_max varchar [note: 'The maximum substandard table rating (expressed as a letter A–P or numeric percentage, e.g., Table D or 150%) eligible for automatic cession under this limit. Risks with table ratings exceeding this threshold require facultative submission regardless of face amount.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this retention limit record was last modified. Tracks changes to limit amounts, effective dates, or status. Supports audit trail and change management requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Sequential version number of this retention limit record. Incremented each time the limit is revised. Enables tracking of limit changes over time and supports point-in-time queries for historical cession routing validation and audit purposes.']

  Note: 'Consolidated reference table defining Life Insurance\'s net retention limits and automatic binding limits by treaty, plan code, risk class, age band, and policy year. Captures limit type (retention per life, retention per policy, automatic binding limit, jumbo limit), limit amount, effective date, and applicable treaty. Includes automatic binding limits per treaty — the maximum face amount that can be automatically ceded without facultative submission — with age/sex/risk class bands and jumbo thresholds. Drives the cession routing decision: risks within retention are kept, risks within automatic binding limits are auto-ceded, and risks exceeding jumbo limits require facultative submission. This is the single source of truth for all retention and automatic binding limit reference data. Supports NAR-based cession calculations and treaty compliance.'
}

  collateral_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The dollar value of collateral posted to support the funds withheld arrangement for credit for reinsurance eligibility. May equal the withheld balance or represent supplemental collateral for unauthorized reinsurers.']
  collateral_type varchar [note: 'Type of collateral arrangement supporting the funds withheld balance for credit for reinsurance purposes. Funds withheld itself serves as collateral; additional collateral types may apply for unauthorized reinsurers.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this funds withheld record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance reporting requirements.']
  credited_interest_rate decimal(8,6) [note: 'The contractually agreed annual interest rate credited by Life Insurance to the reinsurer on the funds withheld balance. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.045000 for 4.5%). Defined in the treaty and may be fixed or index-linked.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this record (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP). Supports multi-currency treaty arrangements with international reinsurers.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which the funds withheld arrangement became effective under the treaty. Marks the start of the period during which Life Insurance retains assets backing ceded reserves.']
  experience_refund_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The experience refund amount due to or from the reinsurer under the treaty for the current period, reflecting favorable or unfavorable claims experience relative to treaty expectations. Impacts net settlement under funds withheld arrangements.']
  interest_accrual_frequency varchar [note: 'The frequency at which interest is accrued and credited on the funds withheld balance as specified in the treaty. Determines the compounding schedule for interest credited amount calculations.']
  interest_credited_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The dollar amount of interest credited to the reinsurer on the funds withheld balance for the current reporting period. Calculated as the withheld balance multiplied by the credited interest rate for the applicable period.']
  interest_rate_basis varchar [note: 'The basis on which the credited interest rate is determined under the treaty. Fixed rates are contractually set; floating rates may reference SOFR or Treasury benchmarks; portfolio rates reflect Life Insurance\'s investment portfolio yield.']
  investment_portfolio_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the specific investment portfolio within Life Insurance\'s general account that holds the assets backing the funds withheld balance. Used for ALM and investment domain coordination via Charles River IMS or SimCorp Dimension.']
  modco_reserve_adjustment decimal(18,2) [note: 'The period-over-period change in the ceded reserve amount under the modified coinsurance arrangement. Represents the increase or decrease in the withheld balance driven by actuarial reserve movements, used in ModCo settlement calculations.']
  net_settlement_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The net cash amount exchanged between Life Insurance and the reinsurer during the settlement period, reflecting changes in the withheld balance, interest credited, reinsurance premiums, and claim recoverables. Positive indicates payment to reinsurer; negative indicates receipt from reinsurer.']
  opening_balance_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The funds withheld balance at the beginning of the current reporting period (BOY or period start). Used to reconcile period-over-period changes in the withheld account and support ALM reporting.']
  rbc_credit_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the funds withheld arrangement qualifies for credit for reinsurance under RBC calculations. Eligibility depends on collateral adequacy, reinsurer domicile, and treaty structure per NAIC RBC guidelines.']
  recapture_date date [note: 'The effective date on which the cession was recaptured, resulting in the release of the funds withheld balance. Populated only when recapture_flag is true.']
  recapture_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the underlying cession has been recaptured by Life Insurance, triggering release of the funds withheld balance back to Life Insurance and termination of the withheld arrangement.']
  record_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier for this funds withheld record, used in bordereaux reporting, settlement statements, and reinsurer correspondence. Assigned by the reinsurance management system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS, RGA AURA).']
  reinsurance_premium_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The reinsurance premium amount due to the reinsurer for the current period under the treaty, netted against the funds withheld balance during settlement. Represents the cost of ceded coverage.']
  settlement_date date [note: 'The actual or scheduled date on which the net settlement of the funds withheld balance is processed between Life Insurance and the reinsurer for the current period.']
  settlement_frequency varchar [note: 'The contractual frequency at which net settlement of the funds withheld account occurs between Life Insurance and the reinsurer. Governs cash flow timing for ALM and treasury coordination.']
  settlement_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the funds withheld balance settlement. Indicates whether the withheld amount has been fully settled with the reinsurer, partially settled, remains open, is under dispute, or has been cancelled.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the operational source system from which this funds withheld record originated (e.g., SWISS_RE_IRIS, RGA_AURA, FAST_REINS). Supports data lineage and ETL reconciliation in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.']
  source_system_ref varchar [note: 'The native record identifier or reference number assigned by the source reinsurance management system (e.g., Swiss Re IRIS fund withheld account ID, RGA AURA withheld balance reference). Enables traceability back to the system of record.']
  termination_date date [note: 'The date on which the funds withheld arrangement was terminated or the withheld balance was fully released to the reinsurer. Null if the arrangement remains active.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this funds withheld record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks silver layer.']
  valuation_date date [note: 'The as-of date for which the funds withheld balance and associated interest calculations are measured. Typically corresponds to a month-end, quarter-end, or year-end actuarial valuation cycle.']
  withheld_asset_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the asset type retained by Life Insurance backing the funds withheld balance. Determines ALM treatment and investment domain coordination requirements for the withheld asset pool.']
  withheld_balance_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total dollar amount of assets retained by Life Insurance on behalf of the reinsurer as of the valuation date.   withheld_balance_change_reason varchar [note: 'The business reason for a change in the funds withheld balance during the current period. Supports audit trail and reconciliation of period-over-period balance movements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new_cession|reserve_increase|reserve_decrease|recapture|termination|correction|interest_accrual|claim_settlement — promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Tracks funds withheld balances under modified coinsurance (ModCo) and funds withheld coinsurance treaties, where Life Insurance retains the assets backing ceded reserves rather than transferring them to the reinsurer.   Note: 'This association product represents the credit risk assumptions applied to each reinsurer for reserve credit calculations and RBC reporting. It captures the specific credit rating, collateral requirements, and RBC credit percentage that apply to a reinsurer under a given assumption set. Each record links one reinsurer to one assumption set with attributes that exist only in the context of this credit risk evaluation relationship. Used for NAIC Schedule S Part 6 reporting and statutory reserve credit calculations.. Existence Justification: In life insurance reinsurance operations, a single reinsurer is evaluated under multiple assumption sets over time as credit ratings change, regulatory frameworks evolve (GAAP/SAP/IFRS), and valuation purposes differ (best estimate vs prudent estimate). Conversely, a single assumption set applies credit risk parameters to multiple reinsurers simultaneously for reserve credit calculations and RBC reporting. The business actively manages these credit assumptions as operational records for NAIC Schedule S Part 6 compliance and statutory reserve credit eligibility.'

  Note: 'This association product represents the analytical relationship between reinsurance treaties and actuarial experience studies. It captures treaty-specific experience metrics (A/E ratios, credibility weights, adjustment factors) derived from experience studies that analyze multiple treaties simultaneously or track a single treaty across multiple study periods. Each record links one treaty to one experience study with metrics that exist only in the context of this specific treaty-study combination.. Existence Justification: In life insurance reinsurance operations, actuaries conduct experience studies that analyze multiple treaties simultaneously (e.g., all YRT treaties in a mortality study), and each treaty requires analysis across multiple experience studies over time (mortality, lapse, expense studies, plus periodic updates). The relationship captures treaty-specific metrics (A/E ratios, credibility weights, adjustment factors) that exist only in the context of a specific treaty-study combination and are used for experience refund calculations and treaty-specific assumption updates.'

  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this reserve calculation record was last modified. Audit trail field for tracking changes.']
  valuation_date date [note: 'The as-of date for this reserve calculation. Typically end-of-year (EOY) or end-of-quarter (EOQ) for statutory and GAAP reporting.']

  Note: 'Core actuarial reserve calculation records capturing GAAP, SAP, and IFRS 17 reserve amounts computed per policy cohort or model segment. Stores net premium reserve (NPR), gross premium reserve (GPR), IBNR, PBR deterministic reserve (DR), stochastic reserve (SR), and LDTI liability for future policy benefits (LFPB). Includes point-in-time snapshot data: BOY and EOY reserve balances, net amount at risk (NAR), reserve per unit, and reserve change components (new business, terminations, interest accretion, assumption unlocking). Each record is linked to a parent valuation_run, assumption_set, cohort_definition, and pbr_model_segment. Sourced from Prophet/AXIS/MoSes valuation runs. Represents the primary output of the actuarial valuation cycle for statutory annual statement, GAAP financial close, and IFRS 17 reporting.'
}

  exclusion_criteria varchar [note: 'Description of policies or data excluded from the study population (e.g., \'Policies in grace period\', \'Reinsured policies\', \'Policies with incomplete data\', \'First-year policies\'). Documents scope limitations and data quality filters.']
  expected_events decimal(18,4) [note: 'Total number of expected events based on current assumption tables applied to the study population exposure. Used as the benchmark for actual-to-expected (A/E) ratio calculation.']
  exposure_amount decimal(20,2) [note: 'Total exposure measure for the study population, typically expressed in policy-years, life-years, or face amount-years depending on the study type. Denominator for calculating experience rates.']
  impact_on_capital_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Estimated financial impact (in USD) on Risk-Based Capital (RBC) or economic capital if the recommended assumption adjustments are adopted. Used for capital planning and solvency assessment.']
  impact_on_reserves_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Estimated financial impact (in USD) on statutory or GAAP reserves if the recommended assumption adjustments are adopted. Positive values indicate reserve increases; negative values indicate reserve decreases. Used for materiality assessment and management decision-making.']
  materiality_threshold_met_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator (True/False) of whether the experience study results exceed the company\'s materiality threshold for assumption changes. True indicates that the variance is material and requires formal assumption update; False indicates variance is within acceptable tolerance.']
  modified_by_user varchar [note: 'User ID or name of the actuary or analyst who last modified this experience study record. Audit trail for change tracking and accountability.']

  lapse_rate_assumption decimal(5,4) [note: 'The assumed annual lapse or surrender rate used in the reserve calculation. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0500 for 5.00%).']
  ldti_transition_adjustment decimal(18,2) [note: 'The cumulative adjustment to reserves resulting from the adoption of LDTI (Long Duration Targeted Improvements) under FASB ASC 944. Captures the impact of transitioning to updated GAAP reserve methodologies.']
  mortality_assumption_table varchar [note: 'The mortality table used in the reserve calculation. Examples include 2017 CSO, 2001 VBT, or company-specific experience tables.']
  nar decimal(18,2) [note: 'The net amount at risk for the insurer, calculated as the death benefit minus the account value or reserve. Key metric for mortality risk exposure.']
  net_reserve decimal(18,2) [note: 'The net reserve after reinsurance cessions. Calculated as reserve_balance minus reinsurance_ceded_reserve.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes or comments regarding this reserve snapshot. May include explanations of unusual variances, assumption changes, or special considerations.']
  pbr_deterministic_reserve decimal(18,2) [note: 'The deterministic reserve calculated under PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20. One component of the PBR reserve calculation.']
  pbr_net_premium_reserve decimal(18,2) [note: 'The net premium reserve calculated under PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20. Serves as a floor for the PBR reserve.']
  pbr_stochastic_reserve decimal(18,2) [note: 'The stochastic reserve calculated under PBR (Principle-Based Reserving) per VM-20 using scenario modeling. One component of the PBR reserve calculation.']
  product_code varchar [note: 'The insurance product code for which reserves are being held. Examples include WL (Whole Life), UL (Universal Life), IUL (Indexed Universal Life), VUL (Variable Universal Life), Term, SPIA (Single Premium Immediate Annuity), FIA (Fixed Indexed Annuity).']
  reinsurance_ceded_reserve decimal(18,2) [note: 'The portion of the reserve that has been ceded to reinsurers under reinsurance treaties. Reduces the net reserve liability for the ceding company.']
  reporting_period varchar [note: 'The reporting period this snapshot represents. BOY (Beginning of Year), EOY (End of Year), quarterly (Q1-Q4), or monthly. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BOY|EOY|Q1|Q2|Q3|Q4|Monthly — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  reserve_adequacy_status varchar [note: 'The assessment of whether the reserve is adequate to cover expected future obligations. Adequate indicates sufficiency, Deficient indicates shortfall requiring premium deficiency reserve, Redundant indicates excess, Under Review indicates pending actuarial analysis.']
  reserve_balance decimal(18,2) [note: 'The total reserve amount held for this policy or cohort at the snapshot date. Represents the actuarial liability under the specified valuation basis.']
  reserve_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the reserve being captured. Policy Reserve for contract liabilities, Claim Reserve for known claims, Premium Deficiency Reserve for loss recognition, IBNR (Incurred But Not Reported) for estimated unreported claims, Unearned Premium Reserve for prepaid premiums, or Additional Reserve for supplemental reserves.']
  snapshot_date date [note: 'The valuation date for which this reserve snapshot was calculated. Typically BOY (Beginning of Year) or EOY (End of Year) reporting date.']
  valuation_basis varchar [note: 'The accounting or regulatory basis under which the reserve was calculated. GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), SAP (Statutory Accounting Principles), IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards), PBR (Principle-Based Reserving per VM-20), or Tax basis.']

  Note: 'Point-in-time reserve balance snapshots capturing BOY and EOY reserve positions by product, valuation basis, and reporting period. Includes DAC-related actuarial calculation inputs that feed into finance.dac_amortization for GAAP booking. This is the actuarial calculation output; finance.dac_amortization is the SSOT for the accounting entry.'
}

  test_date date [note: 'Date on which the tax qualification test was performed. Represents the business event date for the test calculation.']
  test_notes varchar [note: 'Free-form notes and comments regarding the tax qualification test. Used to document special circumstances, assumptions, or actuarial judgments.']
  test_number varchar [note: 'Business identifier for the tax qualification test. Human-readable reference number used for tracking and audit purposes.']
  test_reason varchar [note: 'Business reason or trigger for performing the tax qualification test. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new_business|policy_change|annual_review|premium_increase|benefit_increase|rider_addition|regulatory_audit|system_migration — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  test_result varchar [note: 'Outcome of the tax qualification test. Pass = policy meets IRC requirements, Fail = policy violates IRC limits, Conditional Pass = policy passes with conditions or adjustments, Not Applicable = test not required for this policy type or scenario.']
  test_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the tax qualification test. Pending = test scheduled but not started, In Progress = test calculation underway, Completed = test finished successfully, Failed = test execution error, Overridden = test result manually adjusted by actuarial or compliance.']
  test_system_source varchar [note: 'Source system or platform that generated the tax qualification test results (e.g., Policy Administration System, Actuarial Valuation System, Prophet, AXIS, MoSes).']
  test_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise timestamp when the tax qualification test calculation was executed. Used for audit trail and sequencing of multiple tests on the same date.']
  test_type varchar [note: 'Type of tax qualification test performed.   assumption_subtype varchar [note: 'Granular subtype within the assumption type. Examples: qx (mortality rate), lapse_rate, disability_incidence, per_policy_expense, credited_rate, credibility_weight. Provides additional specificity for the assumption being modeled.']

  assumption_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier for this assumption detail record. Supports assumption change tracking and audit trails. Examples: v1.0, v2.1, 2024Q1.']
  attained_age varchar [note: 'The attained age of the insured for which this assumption rate applies. Used for age-based segmentation in mortality, lapse, and morbidity assumptions. Null if assumption is not age-dependent.']
  comments varchar [note: 'Free-text comments or notes regarding this assumption detail record. Used for documenting rationale, special considerations, or assumptions about the assumption.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this assumption detail record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.']
  credibility_factor decimal(5,4) [note: 'Credibility weight applied to company experience versus industry tables. Value between 0 and 1, where 1 represents full credibility to company experience. Used in PBR credibility blending calculations.']
  data_source_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the data source or experience study that supports this assumption detail. Examples: experience_study_2023_Q4, SOA_2017CSO, company_mortality_study_2022, industry_lapse_benchmark.']
  distribution_channel varchar [note: 'Distribution channel for which this assumption rate applies. Examples: career_agent, independent_broker, direct, worksite, bank. Used for channel-based lapse and expense segmentation. Null if assumption is channel-neutral.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this assumption detail record becomes effective. Used for assumption versioning and time-based assumption changes.']
  experience_adjustment_factor decimal(10,6) [note: 'Multiplicative adjustment factor applied to base assumption rates based on company experience studies. Values greater than 1 increase the base rate; values less than 1 decrease it. Null if no experience adjustment is applied.']
  expiration_date date [note: 'The date on which this assumption detail record expires or is superseded. Null for currently active assumptions with no planned expiration.']
  face_amount_band varchar [note: 'Face amount band or size category for which this assumption rate applies. Examples: 0-50k, 50k-100k, 100k-250k, 250k-500k, 500k+. Used for size-based lapse and expense segmentation. Null if assumption is size-neutral.']
  gender varchar [note: 'Gender classification for which this assumption rate applies. M=Male, F=Female, U=Unisex or Unknown. Used for gender-based segmentation in mortality and morbidity assumptions. Null if assumption is gender-neutral.']
  geographic_region varchar [note: 'Geographic region or state code for which this assumption rate applies. Used for regional mortality and lapse segmentation. Null if assumption is geography-neutral.']
  issue_age_band varchar [note: 'Issue age band for which this assumption rate applies. Examples: 18-30, 31-40, 41-50, 51-60, 61-70, 71+. Used for issue-age-based segmentation in lapse and mortality assumptions. Null if assumption is issue-age-neutral.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this assumption detail record was last modified. Supports change tracking and audit trail requirements.']
  margin_percentage decimal(7,4) [note: 'Margin percentage added to the base assumption for conservatism or profit loading. Expressed as a percentage. Used in pricing and reserve calculations to provide cushion above best-estimate assumptions.']
  model_platform varchar [note: 'The actuarial modeling platform or system that uses or generated this assumption detail. Examples: Prophet, AXIS, MoSes, GGY, internal_model. Supports traceability to modeling systems.']
  mortality_improvement_scale varchar [note: 'Mortality improvement scale applied to the base mortality table. Examples: Scale_G2, Scale_AA, Scale_BB, none. Applicable for mortality assumption types with projected improvements.']
  mortality_table_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the base mortality table used for this assumption detail. Examples: 2017CSO, 2001VBT, 2008VBT, 2015VBT, company_experience_table. Applicable for mortality assumption types.']
  policy_duration varchar [note: 'The policy duration (years since issue) for which this assumption rate applies. Used for duration-based segmentation in lapse and mortality assumptions. Null if assumption is not duration-dependent.']
  product_segment_code varchar [note: 'Product segment or product type code for which this assumption rate applies. Examples: term, whole_life, universal_life, indexed_universal_life, variable_universal_life. Enables product-specific assumption calibration. Null if assumption applies across all products.']
  rate_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the rate_value. Clarifies whether the value is a percentage, decimal fraction, currency amount, per-thousand rate, per-policy amount, or per-unit cost.']
  rate_value decimal(18,10) [note: 'The numeric assumption value for this detail record. Interpretation depends on assumption_type: mortality qx, lapse percentage, expense dollar amount, interest rate percentage, credibility factor. Supports high precision for actuarial calculations.']
  regulatory_basis varchar [note: 'The regulatory or accounting framework for which this assumption detail is intended. Examples: GAAP, SAP (Statutory Accounting Principles), IFRS17, PBR (Principle-Based Reserving), VM-20, tax compliance.']
  smoker_status varchar [note: 'Smoking status classification for which this assumption rate applies. Used for risk-class segmentation in mortality assumptions. Null if assumption is not smoker-status-dependent.']
  underwriting_class varchar [note: 'Underwriting risk class for which this assumption rate applies. Examples: preferred_plus, preferred, standard, substandard, rated. Used for risk-based segmentation in mortality and lapse assumptions. Null if assumption is class-neutral.']
  valuation_date date [note: 'The valuation date for which this assumption detail is calibrated or applicable. Typically aligns with the valuation run date or experience study period end date.']

  Note: 'Typed detail records under an assumption set capturing individual assumption values by assumption type (mortality, lapse, morbidity, expense, interest rate, credibility). Stores rate values by age, duration, gender, risk class, and other segmentation dimensions. Each row is typed (mortality qx, lapse rate, expense per-policy, credited rate, etc.) and linked to its parent assumption_set. Replaces the need for separate mortality_table, lapse_assumption, disability_assumption, expense_assumption, interest_rate_assumption, and credibility_factor products while preserving full granularity. Supports PBR credibility blending, experience study updates, and pricing model calibration.'
}

  table_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the mortality table: active (currently in use), superseded (replaced by newer table), archived (historical reference only), pending_approval (awaiting regulatory or actuarial approval), or withdrawn (no longer valid).']
  table_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the mortality table by its intended actuarial use: valuation (statutory reserve calculations), pricing (product development), underwriting (risk assessment), experience (company-specific studies), reinsurance (treaty pricing), or illustration (sales projections).']

Table actuarial.alm_strategy {
  alm_strategy_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each cohort-portfolio ALM strategy pairing. Primary key.']
  cohort_definition_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the liability cohort being backed by this ALM strategy']
  portfolio_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the investment portfolio backing this cohort under this ALM strategy']
  alm_strategy_type varchar [note: 'The type of ALM strategy employed for this cohort-portfolio pairing: cash_flow_matching (match liability cash flows), duration_matching (match modified duration), immunization (match duration and convexity), dynamic_hedging (active derivative overlay), liability_driven_investment (LDI approach).']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date on which this ALM strategy pairing became effective. Supports historical tracking of ALM strategy changes over time.']
  investment_committee_approval_date date [note: 'The date on which the investment committee formally approved this ALM strategy pairing. Required for governance and audit trail.']
  last_rebalancing_date date [note: 'The date on which this cohort-portfolio pairing was last rebalanced to target allocation. Used to track rebalancing frequency and compliance.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes documenting the rationale, constraints, or special considerations for this specific cohort-portfolio ALM strategy pairing.']
  rebalancing_threshold_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The maximum allowable percentage drift from the target allocation before rebalancing is triggered for this cohort-portfolio pairing. Specific to this ALM strategy.']
  strategy_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this ALM strategy pairing: active (currently in force), pending_approval (awaiting investment committee approval), suspended (temporarily inactive), terminated (no longer in use).']
  target_allocation_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage of the cohort\'s liabilities that should be backed by this specific portfolio. Multiple portfolios may back a single cohort, with allocation percentages summing to 100%.']
  target_duration_years decimal(6,2) [note: 'The target modified duration in years for the portfolio to match the liability duration of the cohort. This is the core ALM matching metric to manage interest rate risk.']
  termination_date date [note: 'The date on which this ALM strategy pairing was terminated or superseded. Null if currently active. Supports historical tracking.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the operational Asset-Liability Management (ALM) strategy linking liability cohorts to investment portfolios. Each record captures the strategic pairing of a cohort_definition (representing insurance liabilities under LDTI/IFRS 17) to a portfolio (representing backing assets), including target duration matching, allocation weights, rebalancing rules, and effective dates. This is the core operational mechanism by which life insurers match liability cash flows to asset portfolios to manage interest rate risk, liquidity risk, and regulatory capital requirements.. Existence Justification: Life insurers operationally manage Asset-Liability Management (ALM) by strategically pairing liability cohorts (LDTI/IFRS 17 groups) to investment portfolios with matching duration and risk profiles. A single cohort is routinely backed by multiple portfolios for diversification across asset classes (e.g., fixed income, equity, alternatives), and a single portfolio commonly backs multiple cohorts for operational efficiency and scale. The ALM function actively creates, monitors, and rebalances these pairings with specific target durations, allocation weights, rebalancing thresholds, and effective dates.'
}

  approval_date date [note: 'The date on which this specific assumption set application to this product plan was formally approved by the appointed actuary or actuarial committee. Tracks product-specific approval rather than global assumption set approval.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this assumption application record was created in the system.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this assumption set becomes effective for use with this specific product plan. Moved from assumption_set because effective dates vary by product application.']
  expiration_date date [note: 'The date on which this assumption set ceases to be valid for this specific product plan. Null indicates ongoing applicability. Moved from assumption_set because expiration dates vary by product application.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this assumption application record was last modified.']
  override_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this assumption application includes product-specific overrides or adjustments to the base assumption set parameters.']
  override_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text description of any product-specific assumption overrides or adjustments applied in this assumption application.']
  regulatory_basis varchar [note: 'The regulatory or accounting framework this assumption application supports for this product: GAAP, SAP (Statutory Accounting Principles), IFRS17, Tax, or Solvency II. Moved from assumption_set because regulatory basis varies by product and jurisdiction.']
  usage_purpose varchar [note: 'The specific purpose for which this assumption set is applied to this product plan: valuation (reserve calculations), pricing (new product development), illustration (sales support), experience_study (assumption review), repricing (rate adjustment), regulatory_filing (compliance reporting).']

  Note: 'This association product represents the application of actuarial assumption sets to specific product plans. It captures the effective period, regulatory basis, usage purpose, and approval status for each assumption set applied to each product plan. Each record links one assumption_set to one product_plan with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, enabling assumption governance, regulatory compliance tracking, and product-specific assumption management across valuation, pricing, and illustration purposes.. Existence Justification: In life insurance actuarial operations, assumption sets are applied to multiple products across different purposes (pricing, valuation, illustration), and each product uses multiple assumption sets for different regulatory bases (GAAP, SAP, IFRS17) and business purposes. Actuaries actively manage these applications with product-specific effective dates, approval workflows, and override parameters. This is a core operational relationship in assumption governance.'
}

  data_version varchar [note: 'The specific version or edition of the vendor data source used in this assumption set (e.g., \'2017 CSO\', \'Q3 2024 Lapse Study\', \'LIMRA 2023 Expense Benchmark\')']
  incorporation_date date [note: 'The date when this vendor data source was incorporated into the assumption set']
  license_cost_amount decimal(15,2) [note: 'The total annual or one-time license cost for this vendor data source, used in conjunction with cost_allocation_percentage for expense tracking']
  license_end_date date [note: 'The expiration date of the license to use this vendor data source, after which usage must cease or be renewed']
  license_start_date date [note: 'The effective date from which the insurer is licensed to use this vendor data source in actuarial calculations']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes documenting special considerations, restrictions, or context for this vendor data source usage (e.g., \'approved for term products only\', \'requires annual recalibration\')']
  usage_scope varchar [note: 'Description of the permitted usage scope for this vendor data source (e.g., \'valuation only\', \'pricing and valuation\', \'internal use only\', \'regulatory filing permitted\')']
  vendor_contact_name varchar [note: 'The name of the vendor representative or account manager responsible for this data source licensing relationship']

  Note: 'This association product represents the data sourcing relationship between actuarial assumption sets and external vendor data providers. It captures the licensing, usage scope, and cost allocation for vendor-supplied data (mortality tables, lapse studies, expense benchmarks) incorporated into assumption sets. Each record links one assumption set to one vendor data source with attributes governing the terms of use, effective periods, and financial arrangements specific to that data usage relationship.. Existence Justification: In life insurance actuarial operations, assumption sets routinely incorporate data from multiple external vendors (SOA mortality tables, RGA lapse studies, LIMRA expense benchmarks, reinsurer assumptions), and each vendor\'s data products are used across multiple assumption sets for different product lines, valuation dates, and regulatory bases. The business actively manages these data sourcing relationships with specific license terms, usage restrictions, cost allocations, and version tracking that belong to neither the assumption set nor the vendor alone.'
}

Table actuarial.scenario_set {
  scenario_set_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for scenario_set']
  base_scenario_set_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing FK on scenario_set (base_scenario_set_id)']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the scenario set was formally approved for use by the appropriate governance authority.']
  approved_by varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the individual or committee who approved this scenario set for production use.']
  calibration_date date [note: 'Date as of which the scenario set was calibrated to market conditions and economic data.']
  confidence_level decimal(5,4) [note: 'Statistical confidence level for scenario set results, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.9500 for 95% confidence). Used in CTE (Conditional Tail Expectation) calculations.']
  created_by_user varchar [note: 'User identifier or name of the individual who created this scenario set record.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this scenario set record was first created in the system.']
  credit_spread_model varchar [note: 'Name of the credit spread model used for corporate bond scenarios in the set.']
  documentation_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to detailed documentation, methodology papers, or model validation reports for this scenario set.']
  economic_scenario_generator varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the economic scenario generator software or model used to produce this scenario set (e.g., Conning, Milliman GEMS, Moody\'s RiskIntegrity).']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'Date after which this scenario set is no longer valid or approved for use. Null for open-ended scenario sets.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'Date from which this scenario set becomes effective and available for use in actuarial models.']
  equity_model varchar [note: 'Name of the equity return model used in the scenario set (e.g., Geometric Brownian Motion, Regime-Switching).']
  esg_version varchar [note: 'Version number or release identifier of the economic scenario generator used.']
  geographic_scope varchar [note: 'Geographic market or region for which the scenario set is calibrated, using 3-letter country codes or scope descriptors.']
  interest_rate_model varchar [note: 'Name of the interest rate model used in the scenario set (e.g., Cox-Ingersoll-Ross, Hull-White, Black-Karasinski).']
  mean_reversion_parameter decimal(8,6) [note: 'Mean reversion speed parameter used in interest rate or economic models, if applicable.']
  modeling_purpose varchar [note: 'Primary business purpose for which this scenario set is designed: valuation, pricing, forecasting, capital planning, risk management, or regulatory reporting.']
  modified_by_user varchar [note: 'User identifier or name of the individual who last modified this scenario set record.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this scenario set record was last modified or updated.']
  next_review_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next periodic review or recalibration of this scenario set.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-form text field for additional notes, comments, or special considerations regarding this scenario set.']
  product_line_applicability varchar [note: 'Insurance product lines for which this scenario set is designed or approved (e.g., term life, universal life, variable annuities, fixed annuities).']
  projection_horizon_years varchar [note: 'Number of years into the future that scenarios in this set project, representing the modeling time horizon.']
  regulatory_framework varchar [note: 'Regulatory or accounting framework this scenario set supports: GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), Statutory (SAP), IFRS 17, VM-20 (Valuation Manual), C-3 Phase I/II, ORSA (Own Risk and Solvency Assessment), Solvency II, or none.']
  risk_neutral_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the scenario set uses risk-neutral (market-consistent) assumptions (True) or real-world assumptions (False).']
  scenario_count varchar [note: 'Total number of individual scenarios included in this scenario set.']
  scenario_set_code varchar [note: 'Business identifier code for the scenario set, used for external reference and reporting.']
  scenario_set_description varchar [note: 'Detailed description of the scenario set including its purpose, assumptions, and intended use cases.']
  scenario_set_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the scenario set describing its purpose or use case.']
  scenario_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the scenario set by modeling approach: deterministic (single outcome), stochastic (probabilistic), stress test, sensitivity analysis, baseline, or adverse.']
  seed_value varchar [note: 'Random number generator seed value used to produce stochastic scenarios, enabling reproducibility of results.']
  status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the scenario set: draft (under development), approved (validated but not yet active), active (in production use), archived (historical reference), deprecated (no longer recommended), or under review (validation in progress).']
  stochastic_trial_count varchar [note: 'Number of stochastic trials or paths generated for stochastic scenario sets. Null for deterministic scenarios.']
  tail_percentile decimal(5,4) [note: 'Percentile threshold for tail risk analysis (e.g., 0.9000 for 90th percentile), used in CTE and stress testing.']
  time_step_frequency varchar [note: 'Frequency of time steps within scenario projections: monthly, quarterly, annual, or daily intervals.']
  validation_date date [note: 'Date on which the most recent independent validation of this scenario set was completed.']
  validation_status varchar [note: 'Current status of independent model validation for this scenario set.']
  valuation_date date [note: 'Effective date for which this scenario set is intended to be used in actuarial valuations or projections.']
  volatility_assumption decimal(8,4) [note: 'Base volatility assumption used in stochastic modeling, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.1500 for 15% volatility).']

  Note: 'Master reference table for scenario_set. Referenced by scenario_set_id.'
}

  duration_years decimal(8,4) [note: 'The modified duration of the fixed income security expressed in years, measuring the price sensitivity of the bond to changes in interest rates. Core input for ALM duration matching, interest rate risk management, and RBC C-3 (interest rate risk) charge calculations.']
  fair_market_value decimal(20,4) [note: 'The estimated market value of the investment position at the as-of date, representing the price at which the asset could be exchanged between knowledgeable, willing parties. Used for GAAP reporting under FASB ASC 820, separate account unit value calculations, and NAIC Schedule D FMV column.']
  holding_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the investment position. Active indicates the position is currently held; sold indicates the position has been disposed of; matured indicates a fixed income security that has reached its maturity date; defaulted indicates the issuer has defaulted; written_off indicates the position has been fully impaired.']
  impairment_amount decimal(20,4) [note: 'The cumulative impairment loss recognized on the investment position, representing the write-down from amortized cost to estimated recoverable value. Reported in NAIC Schedule D and GAAP financial statements. Null if impairment_flag is false.']
  impairment_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the investment has been identified as other-than-temporarily impaired (OTTI) under FASB ASC 320 or credit-impaired under FASB ASC 326 (CECL). Triggers recognition of impairment loss in the income statement and disclosure in NAIC Schedule D.']
  is_144a_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the security was issued under SEC Rule 144A, allowing resale to Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) without SEC registration. Relevant for liquidity classification, investment policy compliance, and NAIC Schedule D private placement reporting.']
  is_private_placement boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the security is a privately placed instrument not registered with the SEC. Private placements require separate NAIC Schedule D-1 reporting, SVO filing, and may carry higher RBC charges due to reduced liquidity.']
  issuer_country_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the issuer\'s domicile. Used for foreign investment concentration limits, country risk assessment, NAIC Schedule D foreign investment disclosures, and ORSA country risk reporting.']
  issuer_sector varchar [note: 'The economic sector or industry classification of the security issuer using NAIC or GICS taxonomy (e.g., financial, utilities, technology, government, sovereign). Used for sector concentration monitoring, investment policy compliance, and portfolio diversification analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: government|financial|utilities|technology|healthcare|energy|consumer|industrial|real_estate|sovereign — promote to reference product]']
  liquidity_classification varchar [note: 'Classification of the investment\'s liquidity profile indicating how quickly the position can be converted to cash without significant price impact. Used for ALM liquidity stress testing, ORSA liquidity risk reporting, and alternative asset lock-up period management.']
  maturity_date date [note: 'The contractual date on which a fixed income security\'s principal is scheduled to be repaid in full. Used for ALM duration matching, cash flow projection in actuarial valuation systems, and NAIC Schedule D reporting. Null for equity and perpetual instruments.']
  naic_designation varchar [note: 'NAIC credit quality designation assigned to fixed income securities (1 through 6, where 1 is highest quality and 6 is in or near default). Drives statutory reserve requirements, RBC investment risk charges, and investment eligibility under state insurance regulations. Blank for non-fixed-income assets.']
  naic_rbc_factor decimal(8,6) [note: 'The NAIC-prescribed RBC investment risk charge factor applicable to this asset based on its asset class, NAIC designation, and issuer type. Multiplied by the book value or amortized cost to calculate the C-1 (asset default) risk charge component in the RBC formula.']
  naic_schedule_code varchar [note: 'NAIC Annual Statement Schedule classification code indicating which statutory schedule this asset is reported on: D-1 (bonds owned), D-2 (bonds acquired/disposed), E (cash and short-term investments), BA (other long-term invested assets), B (mortgage loans). Mandatory for statutory financial reporting.']
  par_value decimal(20,4) [note: 'The face or nominal value of the security as stated on the instrument, representing the principal amount for bonds or the stated value for equities. Used in NAIC Schedule D reporting, amortized cost calculations, and coupon income accrual.']
  quantity decimal(20,6) [note: 'The number of units, shares, or contracts held for this investment position. For bonds, represents the face amount in units; for equities, the number of shares; for fund interests, the number of units or partnership interests. Core measurement field for the resource.']
  rating_agency varchar [note: 'The Nationally Recognized Statistical Rating Organization (NRSRO) that assigned the credit rating for this security. Required for NAIC SVO cross-reference and regulatory credit quality validation.']
  source_system_code varchar [note: 'The unique identifier assigned to this investment position record in the originating investment management system (e.g., Charles River IMS position ID, SimCorp Dimension holding reference). Used for data lineage, reconciliation between the lakehouse and source systems, and audit trail.']
  unrealized_gain_loss decimal(20,4) [note: 'The difference between the fair market value and the amortized cost (or book value) of the investment position, representing the mark-to-market gain or loss not yet realized through sale. Reported in NAIC Schedule D and used for GAAP OCI reporting under FASB ASC 320.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this asset holding record was most recently updated in the data platform, reflecting the latest valuation refresh, status change, or data correction. Used for incremental data processing and audit trail in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  yield_to_maturity decimal(8,6) [note: 'The total annualized return anticipated on a fixed income security if held to maturity, expressed as a decimal. Used for investment income projection, portfolio yield reporting, and ALM asset-liability spread analysis.']

  Note: 'Represents an individual investment position held within a portfolio at a point in time, covering all asset classes including fixed income, equity, mortgage loans, alternative investments (private equity, hedge funds, real estate, infrastructure), and other Schedule BA assets. Captures CUSIP/ISIN identifier, asset class and subtype, NAIC designation, book value, amortized cost, FMV, par value, quantity/units held, acquisition date, maturity date, coupon/dividend rate, credit rating, NAIC Schedule classification (D-1, D-2, E, BA, B). For mortgage loans: property type, LTV ratio, DSCR, amortization type, loan status, appraisal value. For alternative assets: fund manager, commitment/funded/unfunded amounts, vintage year, investment strategy, liquidity classification, lock-up period. Core operational record for portfolio composition, RBC investment risk charge calculations, and NAIC Schedule reporting across all asset types.'
}

  duration_years decimal(8,4) [note: 'Modified duration of the security expressed in years, measuring price sensitivity to a 1% change in interest rates. Core input for ALM duration matching between general account assets and insurance policy liabilities, and for RBC interest rate risk charge calculations.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date from which the security record became active and eligible for use in trade execution, valuation, and compliance systems. Supports point-in-time reporting and audit trail requirements for NAIC and SEC regulatory submissions.']
  exchange_code varchar [note: 'ISO 10383 Market Identifier Code (MIC) of the primary exchange on which the security is listed (e.g., XNYS for NYSE, XNAS for NASDAQ). Used for trade execution routing in Charles River IMS and market data feed mapping.']
  first_coupon_date date [note: 'Date of the first scheduled coupon payment after issuance. Used to calculate the initial accrued interest period, which may be a short or long first coupon period, for accurate investment income accrual and cash flow modeling.']
  fitch_rating varchar [note: 'Credit quality rating assigned by Fitch Ratings (e.g., AAA, AA+, BBB-, BB+). Used as a third-party credit opinion for NAIC designation determination and investment policy compliance monitoring when Moody\'s or S&P ratings are unavailable or split-rated.']
  gics_industry_group varchar [note: 'Second-level GICS industry group classification providing more granular sector segmentation (e.g., Banks, Insurance, Diversified Financials). Supports detailed sector exposure reporting and investment guideline compliance checks.']
  gics_sector varchar [note: 'Top-level sector classification per the MSCI/S&P Global Industry Classification Standard (GICS) framework (e.g., Financials, Energy, Health Care). Used for sector concentration monitoring, performance attribution, and investment policy compliance in SimCorp Dimension.']
